prescriptive_note: Every requirement below is PRESCRIPTIVE: it states what the modernized system MUST, SHOULD or MAY do, not what the legacy system was observed to do. Where a requirement corrects observed behaviour, the anomaly_details field records what the legacy system actually did and anomaly_resolution records the action taken, resolved against srs-anomaly-resolution-log.json. Every requirement traces to a named Discovery finding with a file and line. No requirement is invented: the one class of requirement with no legacy counterpart is identity, audit and retention, and each of those traces to a named ABSENCE in the Discovery record (BR-090, BR-095, BV-06) rather than to an observed behaviour — that is its evidence.

requirements.description: The system MUST allow an authorized principal to create a student record capturing roll number, first name, last name, date of birth, gender, at least one telephone contact point, a guardian reference, enrolled programme and admission year. The record MUST be persisted atomically together with its audit entry, and MUST NOT be persisted unless every validation rule in REQ-002 through REQ-009 passes.

acceptance_criteria.given: An authorized principal and a datastore containing no record with roll number 'BCA2024001'
acceptance_criteria.when: They submit roll number 'BCA2024001', first name 'Asha', last name 'Mehta', date of birth 2006-04-03, gender 'Female', primary telephone '+919876543210', guardian 'Ravi Mehta', programme 'BCA' and admission year 2024
acceptance_criteria.then: Exactly one student record exists with those values, its lifecycle_state is Active, its created_at and created_by are set from the server clock and the authenticated principal, its row_version is 1, and one AuditEntry with operation Create is written in the same transaction

acceptance_criteria.given: The same principal
acceptance_criteria.when: They submit a record whose first name is empty
acceptance_criteria.then: No student record, contact point, guardian reference, enrolment or audit entry is created, and the failure is reported per REQ-083

acceptance_criteria.given: A submission that passes validation but whose audit write fails
acceptance_criteria.then: The student record is not persisted either, and the principal is told the operation failed

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy create path inserted ten columns in one parameterized statement with no uniqueness pre-check, no field-level validation, no transaction and no audit record. The atomicity clause corrects BR-093: because the legacy insert autocommits and then performs refresh work that can itself fail, a committed row could be reported to the user as a failed save.

requirements.description: The system MUST declare each field's mandatory or optional status explicitly, MUST indicate mandatory fields on the entry surface before submission, and MUST reject a submission missing any mandatory value with an error naming each missing field. Roll number, first name, last name, date of birth, gender, primary telephone, guardian name, programme and admission year are mandatory. No field may become mandatory as a side effect of a runtime fault.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Missing mandatory values are all named
acceptance_criteria.given: An entry surface with first name and gender left empty and all other mandatory fields supplied
acceptance_criteria.then: The response names both 'first name' and 'gender' as missing in one reporting pass, no record is created, and no runtime exception message is shown

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Mandatory status is visible in advance
acceptance_criteria.given: The entry surface before any submission
acceptance_criteria.when: It is inspected visually and programmatically
acceptance_criteria.then: Every mandatory field is marked as such, and the marking is exposed to assistive technology per REQ-106

acceptance_criteria.given: A submission supplying every mandatory field and omitting the alternate telephone
acceptance_criteria.then: The record is created successfully

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy system had no required-field validation at all. The three reference-value selectors were de-facto mandatory only because none had a default selection and all were read via an unguarded member access that raised a null-reference exception, reported by a blanket catch as 'Error: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.' naming no field — and that accidental guard was then defeated from the second create onward because the reset routine could not clear the selectors. The seven text fields were genuinely optional, so a record of entirely empty strings was persistable. The mandatory set prescribed here extends the legacy de-facto set to the identifying and contact fields; it is confirmed against the schema's own Required flag, which was set on roll number alone.

requirements.description: The system MUST validate every input at the system boundary before any persistence attempt, enforcing presence, maximum length, permitted character set and documented format per field. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be trimmed before validation and before persistence. Inner layers MUST trust boundary-validated input and MUST NOT re-validate.

acceptance_criteria.given: A first name submitted as '  Asha  '
acceptance_criteria.when: The record is created and re-read
acceptance_criteria.then: The stored value is exactly 'Asha'

acceptance_criteria.given: A first name submitted as '   '
acceptance_criteria.then: It is rejected as a missing mandatory field, not accepted as a three-character name

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Validation occurs once, at the boundary
acceptance_criteria.given: A service-layer operation invoked with already-validated input
acceptance_criteria.then: No inner layer repeats the boundary validation

requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy values passed straight from the input control into the statement with no trim, no emptiness check, no length check, no character-set check and no format check, and no maximum length was set on any of the thirteen text boxes. The data-flow trace records all three personal-data flows as carrying an implicit encode transformation with 'no normalisation, trimming, casing, length limit or character-set restriction' and 'any text whatsoever is accepted into a telephone field'. The structural assessment states plainly that this is new work: 'Validation is a NEW requirement here, not a port.' The boundary-consolidation clause applies the redundant_validation discipline to where validation lives, so that adding it does not scatter it.

requirements.description: The system MUST carry date of birth end to end as a date-only typed value with no time component and no timezone, and MUST NEVER convert it to, or parse it from, a culture-formatted display string for the purpose of storage or retrieval. Culture formatting MUST occur only at the presentation boundary.

acceptance_criteria.given: A record created with date of birth 2006-04-03 on a host configured day-first
acceptance_criteria.when: It is re-read on a host configured month-first
acceptance_criteria.then: The value is still 3 April 2006; it is not interpreted as 4 March 2006

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No display string reaches the datastore
acceptance_criteria.given: The create and amend paths
acceptance_criteria.when: The value bound for date of birth is inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: It is a typed date, not the display text of any control

acceptance_criteria.given: Any persisted date of birth
acceptance_criteria.then: It carries no time-of-day element

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy create and amend paths both bound the date picker's locale-formatted DISPLAY STRING rather than its typed value into a date column, so the provider had to reparse it under the ambient culture. Day values 1 to 12 transposed silently with no error while 13 to 31 failed loudly, making the corruption selective and hardest to detect exactly where it is most plausible. The data-flow trace records three implicit translate transformations on this one attribute, so a date of birth made two unanchored culture round trips per amend cycle and 'repeated edits across differently configured machines can compound the drift'. The underlying column is a double-precision serial with an 1899-12-30 epoch, no timezone, and permits a time component on a semantically date-only field.

requirements.description: The system MUST store every telephone number as text of sufficient length to hold a full international number including country prefix, MUST NEVER store it in a numeric type, MUST preserve leading zeros, and MUST validate it against a documented format before persistence.

acceptance_criteria.given: An authorized principal
acceptance_criteria.then: The record is created and the value reads back as exactly '9876543210'

acceptance_criteria.given: The same principal
acceptance_criteria.then: It is accepted, normalized per the documented format, and reads back without loss of the country prefix

acceptance_criteria.given: A telephone number submitted as '0123456789'
acceptance_criteria.then: The leading zero is still present

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Non-telephone text is rejected with attribution
acceptance_criteria.given: A telephone field submitted as 'not a number'
acceptance_criteria.then: It is rejected with an error naming the telephone field and the expected format, not with a provider type-mismatch message

requirements.anomaly_details: Both legacy telephone columns were 4-byte signed integers with a ceiling of 2,147,483,647, confirmed by decoding the table definition directly. Every ten-digit Indian mobile number begins with 6, 7, 8 or 9 and was therefore unstorable, and every value actually present in the file is nine digits — truncated or placeholder — which is why db-archaeology judged the project report's claim that a ten-digit number passed testing 'not credible'. Integer storage also silently discarded leading zeros, country prefixes, spaces and plus signs, and the entry form collected the value as unconstrained free text with no length or numeric validation, so the only enforcement was a raw provider error. db-archaeology's remediation is adopted verbatim in principle: phone numbers are identifiers, not arithmetic quantities. Note the unresolved type contradiction recorded in srs-data-model.json: the data-flow trace describes these columns as short text while db-archaeology reports integer, and the data-domain pass rules that 'both are correct about different things, and the mismatch between them IS the defect'.

requirements.description: After a successful create, the system MUST reset every input on the entry surface to its documented initial state, including reference-value selectors, which MUST return to an explicitly unselected state. No value may carry from one record-entry operation into the next.

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal who has just created a record with gender 'Female', programme 'MCA' and admission year 2024
acceptance_criteria.then: All three selectors show no selection, and submitting immediately without choosing them is rejected per REQ-002

acceptance_criteria.given: The same principal creating a second record and supplying only the name fields
acceptance_criteria.then: The submission is rejected for missing gender, programme and admission year; it does not silently adopt the previous record's values

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Date of birth resets to empty
acceptance_criteria.given: The reset surface
acceptance_criteria.then: It holds no value, per REQ-007

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy reset routine cleared the text boxes and reset the date picker to today, then attempted to clear the three selectors by assigning an empty string to their text property. Because all three were closed-list selectors that accept only values present in their item collection, the assignment was silently discarded and the previous selection persisted. From the second create of a session onward every record silently inherited the previous student's gender, programme and admission year unless the operator noticed — and the same defect permanently disabled the accidental mandatory-field guard in BR-011, converting a loud failure into silent wrong data. BR-020 is explicit that this is 'a real data-integrity rule', not a cosmetic defect.

requirements.description: Date of birth MUST have no pre-populated default and MUST be presented as empty until the principal supplies a value. Submission without a date of birth MUST be rejected as a missing mandatory field.

acceptance_criteria.given: A freshly opened entry surface
acceptance_criteria.then: It holds no value and displays no date

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Untouched control is rejected, not accepted
acceptance_criteria.given: A submission in which the principal never touched the date-of-birth control
acceptance_criteria.then: It is rejected naming date of birth as missing; today's date is not persisted

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy date picker had no value, format, minimum or maximum set, so it initialised to the current date, and the reset routine explicitly re-set it to today. A principal who did not touch the control therefore submitted today as the student's date of birth — BR-021 describes this as 'a plausible-looking value that is always wrong'. No downstream check could distinguish an untouched control from a deliberate entry, which is why a blank is prescribed rather than a different default.

requirements.description: Roll number MUST be validated as non-empty after trimming, unique under case-insensitive comparison across all non-purged records, and conformant to a documented format. The system MUST detect a collision before attempting to persist and MUST report it as a validation error naming roll number as the conflicting field.

acceptance_criteria.given: An existing record with roll number 'BCA2024001'
acceptance_criteria.when: A principal submits a new record with roll number 'BCA2024001'
acceptance_criteria.then: The submission is rejected with an error naming roll number as already in use, no insert is attempted, and no provider error text is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: An existing record with roll number 'bca2024001'
acceptance_criteria.then: It is rejected as a duplicate

acceptance_criteria.given: A submission with roll number '' or '   '
acceptance_criteria.then: It is rejected as a missing mandatory field; the empty string is never a valid key

requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy roll number was the sole record identifier, typed freely with no format mask, no length limit, no check digit and no generation scheme. Uniqueness rested solely on a database index the application never pre-checked, so a collision surfaced only as an untriaged provider error. The column permitted the empty string because AllowZeroLength was true, so BR-012 records that an empty roll number was accepted once and then blocked all further empty-string inserts. Two Pass-1 passes disagreed about whether the index exists at all, and the data-domain pass rates the consequence critical as BV-01. Case-insensitive uniqueness is prescribed because BR-092 shows the legacy case-sensitive index and case-insensitive query clause disagree, which BR-037 identifies as 'the one configuration in which this rule becomes active'. Recovered values include '1', '2', '3', '34' and '434'. The documented format requires SME confirmation.

requirements.description: Every text attribute MUST declare an explicit maximum length in the requirement set, in the data model and at the input surface, and the three MUST agree. No attribute may be unbounded. A length violation MUST be prevented at the input surface and, if it reaches the service layer, MUST be reported as a validation error naming the field and its limit.

acceptance_criteria.given: An input whose declared maximum is 100 characters
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal attempts to enter 101 characters
acceptance_criteria.then: The surface refuses the excess and announces the limit to assistive technology

acceptance_criteria.given: A service call carrying a 300-character first name
acceptance_criteria.then: It is rejected with an error naming first name and its maximum, not with a provider error

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Guardian name is bounded like other names
acceptance_criteria.given: The guardian name attribute
acceptance_criteria.then: It is bounded, not unlimited

traces_to.line_note: students table definition; TEXT width 510 bytes = 255 characters.

requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy text columns were capped at 255 characters by the binary table definition alone, while the guardian name column was an unbounded long-value type. No maximum length was set on any of the thirteen text boxes and no length check existed in code, so BR-096 records that 'the only length rule in the system lives in the binary table definition and surfaces only as an untriaged error on save'. IM-008 notes the inconsistency has no recorded rationale and that consequently 'the one field holding a third party's personal data is also the one field with no length ceiling'. The accessibility audit records the same absence as A11Y-007, verifying that the string MaxLength occurs zero times in either entry Designer file.

requirements.description: The system MUST allow an authorized principal to retrieve one student record for amendment, addressed by its surrogate identifier. The retrieval MUST NOT be performed during object construction, MUST release every resource it acquires on both the success and the failure path, and MUST NOT leave any shared resource in a state that affects a later operation.

acceptance_criteria.given: An existing Active record
acceptance_criteria.when: An authorized principal opens it for amendment
acceptance_criteria.then: Every attribute is populated from stored data, including reference values and the row version

acceptance_criteria.given: A retrieval that fails part-way through reading the record
acceptance_criteria.then: Every acquired resource is released, the next operation succeeds normally, and no shared state is left degraded

acceptance_criteria.given: The amendment component
acceptance_criteria.then: No datastore call occurs during construction; retrieval is an explicit call that can be guarded

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy retrieval ran inside the form's constructor with no exception guard, invoked from a handler that also had no guard, so every failure mode propagated as an unhandled exception and terminated the application — in contrast to the save path, which was fully wrapped. There was no deterministic-release construct anywhere in the file, so the reader close depended entirely on the happy path: a date-parse failure left an open reader on the shared global connection for the remaining life of the process, which then blocked every other operation because the provider permits only one open reader per connection.

requirements.description: Roll number MUST be immutable after creation. The system MUST NOT offer any path that changes it, and MUST reject a service call attempting to change it. Correcting a mistyped roll number MUST be achievable as a single audited, atomic operation rather than by destroying and recreating the record.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No amendment path changes the key
acceptance_criteria.given: An existing record
acceptance_criteria.then: Roll number is presented as non-editable and is not included in the set of amendable attributes

acceptance_criteria.given: A service call submitting a different roll number for an existing surrogate identifier
acceptance_criteria.then: It is rejected, and the rejection is audited

acceptance_criteria.given: A record whose roll number was mistyped, and a principal authorized to correct it
acceptance_criteria.then: The roll number changes in one transaction, the record is never absent at any point, and an AuditEntry records the prior and new value

requirements.anomaly_details: Immutability itself is CARRIED FORWARD, not corrected: BR-031 describes it as 'the system's strongest and clearest invariant', enforced by a read-only control property plus the shape of the update statement, which omitted the key from its assignment clause and used it only in its predicate. Three things are corrected. First, the legacy enforcement was a read-only text box, which BR-031 notes left the control tab-reachable with its value still posting, so enforcement moves server-side per NFR-021. Second, the legacy field's mutability was context-dependent and defined in two separate Designer files — freely editable on create, read-only on amend — which ANOM-038 consolidates. Third, the legacy system offered no correction route at all except delete-and-recreate, which BR-093 notes 'loses the record entirely in between because there is no transaction and no audit trail'.

requirements.description: The system MUST allow an authorized principal to amend a retrieved student record. It MUST persist only attributes the principal actually changed, MUST submit the row version read with the record, and MUST reject the amendment if that version no longer matches. It MUST NOT silently overwrite a concurrent modification, and MUST NOT write back a value that failed to populate on retrieval.

acceptance_criteria.given: A retrieved record in which the principal changes only the last name
acceptance_criteria.then: The persisted change set contains last name alone, the audit entry records only that attribute's prior and new value, and no other attribute is rewritten

acceptance_criteria.given: Two principals who each retrieved the same record at version 4, and the first has saved so the stored version is now 5
acceptance_criteria.then: The amendment is rejected with a conflict error identifying the attributes the first principal changed, and the stored record is unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: A retrieved record the principal does not modify
acceptance_criteria.then: No attribute is written, the row version does not advance, and no change audit entry is created

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy amendment issued one statement writing all nine non-key columns from current control state regardless of whether the principal changed any of them, with no dirty-field tracking, no concurrency token, no row-version check and no comparison against the loaded values. BR-032 records the consequence precisely: 'merely opening and saving a record can destroy data the user never touched', because any value that failed to populate on load — most importantly a reference selector left blank because its stored value was outside the hardcoded list — was written back as the new truth. Combined with concurrent instances being explicitly permitted, the last save won silently and the loser's edits were destroyed with no warning to either party. The conflict-resolution experience requires SME confirmation per ANOM-010.

requirements.description: When a record holds a reference value absent from the currently active value set, the system MUST still present the record for amendment, MUST display the stored value, MUST mark it as inactive or unrecognised, and MUST preserve it unchanged unless the principal explicitly selects a replacement. The system MUST NOT silently discard a stored value and MUST NOT make a record un-amendable because of the content of a reference field.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Out-of-set value is shown and preserved
acceptance_criteria.given: A record whose programme code is 'BTECH', which is not in the active set
acceptance_criteria.when: An authorized principal opens it, changes only the last name and saves
acceptance_criteria.then: The record is amendable, 'BTECH' is displayed and marked inactive, and after saving the programme code is still 'BTECH'

acceptance_criteria.given: The same record
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal explicitly selects 'BCA' and saves
acceptance_criteria.then: The programme code becomes 'BCA' and the audit entry records the prior value 'BTECH'

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Case difference is not an out-of-set value
acceptance_criteria.given: A record whose gender code is stored as 'male' in lower case
acceptance_criteria.then: It matches the active value 'Male' case-insensitively, is presented as selected and is not marked inactive

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy retrieval populated the three selectors by assigning the stored string to the selected-item property, which performed an exact case-sensitive lookup in a hardcoded list. A value not found was silently ignored and the control left unselected; saving then raised a null-reference exception. BR-033 records the practical rule: any record whose gender, programme or admission year lay outside the hardcoded lists — a 2024 intake, a decommissioned programme, or a value differing only in letter case — was PERMANENTLY un-amendable, reported only as a generic object-reference error. Worse, if the principal selected a replacement value in the blanked selector, the unconditional write-back in BR-032 silently destroyed the original datum; the recovered state machine names this 'the application's main data-destruction path short of deletion'. Because the frozen admission-year list already excluded current intakes, BR-033 notes this rule 'will capture every future record created by any other means'. This requirement also removes the legacy PartiallyLoaded state, recorded as a dead state in srs.json.

requirements.description: On retrieval, the system MUST read date of birth as a typed date without any string conversion or culture-dependent parse, and MUST handle an absent or unparseable stored value as a reportable data condition rather than a fault that terminates the operation.

acceptance_criteria.given: A retrieval of any record
acceptance_criteria.then: No string conversion and no culture-dependent parse occurs between the datastore and the presentation boundary

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Unreadable stored value is reported, not fatal
acceptance_criteria.given: A migrated record whose stored date of birth is absent or cannot be interpreted
acceptance_criteria.then: The record opens, the date-of-birth field is marked as requiring correction, the condition is logged with a correlation identifier, and the application does not terminate

acceptance_criteria.given: A stored date of birth outside the presentation control's displayable range
acceptance_criteria.then: The value is shown or marked as out of range; no unhandled fault occurs

requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy retrieval read the stored date, converted it to a string and parsed it back with a culture-free parse — both under the ambient culture — before assigning it to a control whose setter additionally enforced its own range. BR-034 records three distinct exception modes from this one line, all raised inside a constructor with no handling: a format failure on an empty or unparseable value, and a range failure on a value outside the control's bounds. Because the exception occurred after the reader was opened but before it was closed, it also leaked the reader and poisoned the shared connection for the life of the process. The 'reportable data condition' clause is prescribed because migration cannot assume stored dates are valid: the two live legacy rows are described by db-archaeology as implausible test data.

requirements.description: When a requested record does not exist, the system MUST report that explicitly, MUST NOT present an editable surface for it, and MUST NOT permit a save attempt against it. The absent-record outcome MUST be distinguishable by the principal from a validation failure and from an infrastructure fault.

acceptance_criteria.given: A request to amend an identifier with no matching record
acceptance_criteria.then: The principal is told the record does not exist or is no longer available, and no editable surface is presented

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No blank surface masquerades as the record
acceptance_criteria.given: The same request
acceptance_criteria.then: No surface is shown populated with initial or default values as though it were the requested record

acceptance_criteria.given: A record archived by another principal between the list being read and the amendment being requested
acceptance_criteria.then: The absent-record outcome is reported distinguishably from a validation error

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Save against zero rows cannot report success
acceptance_criteria.given: Any amendment whose write affects zero records
acceptance_criteria.then: It is reported as a failure stating the record no longer exists, never as success

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy retrieval guarded its populate block with a read test and supplied no alternative branch. When no record matched it closed the reader and returned, leaving a surface that appeared to be amending the selected student but held only designer defaults — empty text boxes, unselected selectors and today's date. The condition surfaced later as a generic object-reference error indistinguishable from two other failure modes. Worse, BR-036 records that if the principal filled the blank surface in and saved, 'the UPDATE matches no rows and still reports Record updated successfully because ExecuteNonQuery's zero row count is never checked'. This requirement also removes the legacy BlankEdit state, recorded as a dead state in srs.json.

requirements.description: Every mutation MUST target exactly one record addressed by its surrogate identifier. The system MUST inspect the affected-record count and MUST treat any count other than one as a failure: zero MUST be reported as the record no longer existing, and more than one MUST abort the operation and raise a data-integrity alert. No mutation may report success without having confirmed that exactly one record changed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Exactly one is the success condition
acceptance_criteria.given: A valid amendment to an existing record
acceptance_criteria.then: The affected count is one and success is reported

acceptance_criteria.given: An amendment whose target was archived concurrently
acceptance_criteria.then: The operation is reported as failed, the reason is that the record no longer exists, and the transaction is rolled back

acceptance_criteria.criterion: More than one aborts and alerts
acceptance_criteria.given: A datastore state in which a mutation would affect two records
acceptance_criteria.then: The transaction is rolled back, a data-integrity alert is raised to operations, and the principal is told the operation could not be completed safely

requirements.anomaly_details: Both legacy mutations were keyed on the user-supplied roll number with no row limit, and the affected-row count was discarded in both paths, so an amendment matching no records reported success and a deletion matching nothing reported success too. IM-027 states the consequence: 'the application cannot distinguish a completed change from a no-op'. BR-037 is explicit that the rule was latent rather than active, resting entirely on an index whose existence two Discovery passes disagreed about — 'if the index were ever absent, as one Pass-1 input incorrectly reported, or if data were loaded by another tool, a single Update or Delete action would silently modify or remove every matching record while reporting success'. The data-domain pass rates this BV-01 at critical severity. The discarded count is what made the weak key dangerous rather than merely untidy, because it removed the one signal that would have revealed a multi-row effect.

requirements.description: Any irreversible or destructive operation MUST require explicit confirmation, and the confirmation MUST identify the specific record by roll number and student name. The system MUST warn before discarding unsaved input on navigation away from or closure of an entry surface.

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal archiving the record of 'Asha Mehta', roll number 'BCA2024001'
acceptance_criteria.then: It states both the roll number and the student name, so the principal can verify the correct record before confirming

acceptance_criteria.given: The same confirmation
acceptance_criteria.then: The record is unchanged, no audit entry for an archive is written, and no shared resource is left in a changed state

acceptance_criteria.given: An entry surface with unsaved input
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal navigates away or attempts to close the application
acceptance_criteria.then: They are warned that input will be lost and may cancel

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy confirmation dialog is CARRIED FORWARD in principle — BR-056 records it as the only confirmation gate anywhere in the application — but corrected in substance, because BR-056 also records that 'the dialog names no student, so it cannot be used to verify that the correct record is about to be destroyed'. A confirmation that cannot perform its function is a worse posture than none, because it induces false confidence. The scope is also extended: no other destructive or semi-destructive legacy action asked for confirmation, including the amendment that rewrote all nine attributes and the exit that discarded unsaved entry data with no prompt. Which operations beyond archive and purge warrant a gate requires SME confirmation.

requirements.description: Deletion MUST be logical. The system MUST mark the record as archived, retain it for the configured retention period, exclude it from all default reads and from statistics over the active population, and record the acting principal and instant. Physical destruction MUST occur only through a separately authorized, audited purge that renders the data unrecoverable from the storage medium.

acceptance_criteria.given: An Active record and a principal authorized to archive
acceptance_criteria.then: lifecycle_state becomes Archived, archived_at and retention_expires_at are set, the record no longer appears in default reads or active-population statistics, an AuditEntry with operation Archive is written, and the record remains retrievable by an authorized principal

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Purge is separately authorized and audited
acceptance_criteria.given: An Archived record past its retention expiry and a principal authorized to purge
acceptance_criteria.then: An AuditEntry with operation Purge is written and survives, and the record's field values are not recoverable from the storage medium afterwards

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Archive does not require purge authority
acceptance_criteria.given: A principal authorized to archive but not to purge
acceptance_criteria.then: It is denied and the denial is audited

acceptance_criteria.given: A completed archive
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal immediately views the statistics dashboard
acceptance_criteria.then: The dashboard renders successfully with figures reflecting the archive

corroborating: db-archaeology[orphan-object: deleted records in page slack]

requirements.anomaly_details: Legacy deletion was a hard delete against the sole table with no status column, no archive table, no soft-delete flag, no retention period and no audit of who deleted what or when. Once confirmed, the student's and the named guardian's personal data were irrecoverable from the application. BV-06 rates the absence high and records that it 'forecloses both data-subject-request handling and any reconstruction after an erroneous delete'. The final criterion corrects BR-004 specifically: the legacy delete path contained the application's only connection close, so navigating to the dashboard afterwards raised an unhandled fault and terminated the application. The unrecoverability clause corrects a measured forensic finding — six previously deleted rows were recovered intact from page slack with all ten field values readable — so physical deletion in the legacy system was not merely unaudited but also not actually destructive.

requirements.description: The system MUST present a list of student records to an authorized principal, paged with a bounded maximum page size and ordered by a deterministic, stable sort the principal can change. It MUST NOT read the entire record set into memory at any volume, and MUST exclude archived and purged records from the default list.

acceptance_criteria.given: A datastore containing 5,000 Active records
acceptance_criteria.then: At most one page of records is retrieved, the issued query carries an explicit row limit and offset or cursor, and the principal can navigate to subsequent pages

acceptance_criteria.given: Two consecutive identical page requests with no intervening mutation
acceptance_criteria.then: The records appear in the same order

acceptance_criteria.given: A datastore with 10 Active and 3 Archived records
acceptance_criteria.then: Only the 10 Active records appear, and viewing archived records requires an explicit choice

acceptance_criteria.given: The list
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal selects a different sort attribute
acceptance_criteria.then: The list reorders and the order remains stable across refreshes

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy list bound the entire table with no predicate, no ordering, no row limit and no paging, growing without bound as the table grew, and it was the application's only record-listing mechanism. Display order was whatever physical order the engine returned, which BR-050 notes 'is not guaranteed stable across inserts and deletes, so a user's visual position is not stable'. Every refresh created a new result set and discarded the previous one without disposing it. The exclusion clause is new behaviour enabled by REQ-027: the legacy system had no status attribute to filter on, which is exactly why BR-075 records that all-time and currently-enrolled were the same number by construction.

requirements.description: The system MUST allow an authorized principal to search student records by roll number, first name, last name, guardian name, telephone number, programme and admission year. Every search term MUST be bound as a parameter. Wildcard and pattern characters within a term MUST be escaped so they match literally. Matching MUST be case-insensitive, and the matching rule for each field MUST be documented and consistent.

acceptance_criteria.given: A record for 'Asha Mehta'
acceptance_criteria.then: That record is returned, where the legacy system returned nothing because surname was unsearchable

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Apostrophe in a name is matched literally
acceptance_criteria.given: A record whose last name is "O'Brien"
acceptance_criteria.then: That record is returned, no error occurs and the application does not terminate

acceptance_criteria.given: Any search surface
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal submits a term containing a closing quote followed by a disjunctive always-true predicate
acceptance_criteria.then: The term is matched literally, no record matches, no additional records are returned and no error occurs

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal searching for a term containing a percent sign
acceptance_criteria.then: The percent sign is matched as a character, not interpreted as a wildcard

acceptance_criteria.given: A record whose first name is 'Asha'
acceptance_criteria.then: The record is returned

requirements.anomaly_details: Three defects are corrected together. The legacy predicate concatenated raw keystrokes into the query text with no parameterization and no escaping — the only unparameterized path in the application and its one live injection point, with the grid providing a direct output channel for whatever the altered statement returned. It searched only two of ten attributes, so BR-054 records that 'a user who knows only a student's surname or phone number cannot locate the record except by scrolling the unordered full list', and that no filter by programme or year existed despite those being the dashboard's primary reporting axes. Its two halves behaved under different rules — exact whole-value matching on roll number, substring matching on first name — from a single input box. BR-052 also records that a legitimate apostrophe terminated the literal and crashed the application unhandled, so 'a legitimate Irish or Italian surname in the first-name field is indistinguishable from an injection attempt'.

requirements.description: No query text may be assembled by concatenating or interpolating any value that originated outside the application, on any path, including paths whose interpolated value is currently of a non-injectable type.

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered codebase
acceptance_criteria.when: An automated check scans for query text assembled by concatenation or interpolation
acceptance_criteria.then: It finds none, against a legacy baseline of six such statements of sixteen

acceptance_criteria.given: The statistics computation
acceptance_criteria.then: Admission-year values are bound as parameters, not concatenated as quoted literals, even though the legacy equivalents were not injectable

requirements.anomaly_details: This constraint deliberately covers more than the one exploitable statement. The legacy system had six unparameterized statements: the search, which interpolated raw user input and is the confirmed vulnerability named in ESC-1 as the live exfiltration path for the entire personal-data set, and five dashboard cohort counts which BR-074 notes are 'not injectable despite being concatenated, because the interpolated value is an Integer'. The five are included because the property that makes them safe is incidental to their current implementation, not guaranteed by any rule, and because the engine's lack of statement batching — which bounds the search exposure to unauthorized read — is likewise a property of the legacy engine that a replatform removes.

requirements.description: The system MUST provide an explicit control to clear an active search filter, MUST preserve an active filter across any refresh triggered by an unrelated operation, and MUST indicate to the principal when a filter is active and how many records it matched.

acceptance_criteria.given: An active filter on 'Mehta' and a principal who archives one of the matching records
acceptance_criteria.when: The list refreshes after the archive
acceptance_criteria.then: The filter is still applied and the list shows the remaining matches, not the full record set

acceptance_criteria.given: An active filter
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal uses the clear control
acceptance_criteria.then: The filter is removed and the default list returns; clearing does not require submitting an empty search

acceptance_criteria.given: An active filter matching 3 of 500 records
acceptance_criteria.then: It indicates that a filter is active and that 3 records matched

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Empty term is not a filter
acceptance_criteria.given: An empty or whitespace-only search term
acceptance_criteria.then: The result is the unfiltered default list, equivalent to no filter

requirements.anomaly_details: The blank-search-returns-everything behaviour is CARRIED FORWARD as the semantics of an empty filter, but its role as the only reset mechanism is corrected. The legacy system had no reset control, so BR-053 records that 'clearing the box and pressing Search is therefore the application's only explicit way to clear an active filter'. Worse, because filtering called one loader while every refresh path called a different one that rebound the whole table, IM-026 records that 'a user's filter therefore vanishes without notice whenever anything else happens' — after a deletion, on closing an amendment surface, or on navigation. The resolution is consolidation: one parameterized retrieval path serving every caller, which makes filter survival a property of the design rather than an added feature.

requirements.description: The system SHOULD allow an authorized principal to filter the record list by programme, by admission year and by lifecycle state, and SHOULD make every attribute it displays available as a filter or sort key.

acceptance_criteria.given: A datastore with records across three programmes and four admission years
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal filters by programme 'MCA' and admission year 2024
acceptance_criteria.then: Only records matching both are listed, and the filter composes with the text search in REQ-021

acceptance_criteria.given: The set of attributes the list displays
acceptance_criteria.then: Each is available as a filter or a sort key

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal authorized to view archived records
acceptance_criteria.when: They filter by lifecycle state Archived
acceptance_criteria.then: Archived records are listed and are visibly marked as archived

requirements.anomaly_details: BR-054 records that seven of the ten stored attributes were unsearchable and that 'there is no filter-by-course or filter-by-year capability anywhere in the application despite those being the dashboard's primary reporting axes' — so an operator could see that twelve students were enrolled on a programme but could not list them. The legacy failure mode was also silent: searching an unsearchable attribute returned an empty list 'with no message explaining that the field is not searchable', indistinguishable from no such student. Priority is should rather than must because Discovery evidences the gap but no stakeholder requirement for the specific filter set.

requirements.description: Before offering any operation against a selected record, the system MUST confirm that the selection resolves to an existing record. If no record is selected, the system MUST state that a selection is required. A selection MUST NOT be accepted that does not correspond to stored data.

acceptance_criteria.given: A list with no record selected
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal invokes amend or archive
acceptance_criteria.then: They are told a record must be selected first, and no operation is attempted

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Selection resolves before the operation is offered
acceptance_criteria.given: A selected record archived by another principal a moment earlier
acceptance_criteria.then: The absent-record outcome of REQ-015 is reported; no editable surface opens and no fault occurs

acceptance_criteria.given: The list in any state, including empty
acceptance_criteria.then: Only rows corresponding to stored records are selectable; no placeholder row exists to select

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy selection test is CARRIED FORWARD — BR-055 records that both the amend and the archive path tested for a selection and refused with an advisory message — but it was insufficient, and BR-055 itself notes it was 'the closest thing the application has to an authorization check', a role REQ-061 now takes over. The defect is that the test checked only that something was selected, not that it was a record: BR-060 records that selecting the grid's phantom placeholder row 'passes the selection test in BR-055 and then yields a Nothing roll-number cell', raising an unhandled null-reference exception in both handlers, neither of which had any exception handling.

requirements.description: The unit of operation MUST be one complete student record. The system MUST NOT offer partial-record selection. If bulk operation over multiple records is offered, it MUST require confirmation naming the count and MUST be transactional and audited per record.

acceptance_criteria.given: The record list
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal selects any part of a row
acceptance_criteria.then: The entire record is selected as the unit of operation

acceptance_criteria.given: A selection
acceptance_criteria.then: It applies to exactly one record, consistent with REQ-016

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Bulk operation, if offered, is safe
acceptance_criteria.given: A bulk archive over 12 selected records, if the capability is implemented
acceptance_criteria.then: The confirmation names the count of 12, each record's archive is audited individually, and the whole set commits or rolls back together

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy cardinality is CARRIED FORWARD but made explicit rather than left as a side effect of two presentation properties. BR-059 records that multi-selection was disabled and full-row selection enabled, so 'bulk update and bulk delete are structurally impossible, and there is no select-all, no checkbox column and no batch operation anywhere' — every mutation was a single-record, single-statement, interactive action. That is prescribed as the requirement because it is the cardinality every other requirement here assumes, notably REQ-016. The conditional bulk clause states the conditions under which the constraint could be relaxed without reintroducing BR-037's multi-row hazard; no bulk capability is required.

requirements.description: The record list MUST present only persisted records and MUST NOT render a placeholder or any row not corresponding to stored data. An empty result MUST be presented as an explicit empty state. No interaction with the list may alter displayed data without a corresponding persisted change.

acceptance_criteria.given: A datastore with no Active records
acceptance_criteria.then: It shows an explicit empty-state message and zero rows, so that an empty record set is distinguishable from a populated one

acceptance_criteria.given: A datastore with 7 Active records on the current page
acceptance_criteria.then: There are exactly 7, not 8

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No unpersisted mutation from the list
acceptance_criteria.given: The list
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal presses any key intended to delete or edit in place
acceptance_criteria.then: No displayed data changes, and the list continues to reflect stored data exactly

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy grid was explicitly read-only, but the two properties permitting row addition and deletion were never set and so retained their permissive defaults, which the read-only setting did not suppress. A phantom placeholder row was therefore always rendered, so BR-060 records that 'an empty students table still shows one row, so the grid never looks genuinely empty' and 'any row-count logic over the grid is off by one'. Selecting the placeholder reached a crash path, and pressing the delete key removed rows from the bound in-memory set without touching the datastore, so 'the grid and the data silently disagree until the next reload'. These are behaviours produced by properties never written in source, which is precisely the class of framework magic this SRS converts into a stated requirement.

requirements.description: The record list MUST define its columns explicitly, each carrying a human-readable fully expanded label. Column identity, order, labelling and formatting MUST be declared properties of the presentation layer and MUST NOT be derived from the datastore result-set shape, so that a schema change cannot silently alter the user-facing report or expose a newly added attribute.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Labels are readable, not raw tokens
acceptance_criteria.given: The displayed list
acceptance_criteria.then: They are fully expanded terms such as 'Year of Admission', "Guardian's Name" and 'First Name', not 'YOA', 'FatherName' or 'FName', and each is exposed to assistive technology

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Schema change does not alter the report
acceptance_criteria.given: A new attribute added to the student entity
acceptance_criteria.when: The list is displayed without a presentation change
acceptance_criteria.then: The new attribute does not appear, and no additional column is rendered

acceptance_criteria.given: A displayed date of birth and telephone number
acceptance_criteria.then: Each uses a declared format rather than the default type formatting of the platform

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy grid defined no columns: automatic column generation was enabled at runtime, so column count, order and header text all came from the result set of an unqualified select. Principals therefore saw raw datastore attribute names as headings with no display labels, no formatting, no column hiding and no reordering. BR-061 records the coupling precisely — 'any schema change immediately and silently changes the user-facing report', including exposing a newly added attribute holding sensitive data — and that the code's one use of a physical attribute name coupled the mutation paths to it, so renaming it would break them at runtime. The accessibility audit records the same defect as A11Y-002 at serious severity, noting that a screen reader announces the raw token and that abbreviations are never expanded.

requirements.description: The permitted gender values MUST be held as reference data with exactly one authoritative definition, each carrying a code, a display label, an active flag and a sort position. Every entry surface, validation rule and statistic MUST read the vocabulary from that definition. The initial value set MUST be exactly Male, Female and Other.

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered system
acceptance_criteria.when: Gender values are located in source and data
acceptance_criteria.then: Exactly one definition exists, held as data, against a legacy baseline of literals in two Designer files contradicted by the single place that aggregated them

acceptance_criteria.criterion: All three values are usable end to end
acceptance_criteria.given: A record created with gender 'Other'
acceptance_criteria.then: That record is counted in the gender breakdown, where the legacy system counted it nowhere

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Adding a value requires no rebuild
acceptance_criteria.given: A new gender value added to the reference data
acceptance_criteria.when: The entry surface and statistics are read
acceptance_criteria.then: The new value is selectable and countable with no code change and no redeployment

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy value set was exactly Male, Female and Other, declared as literals in the Designer item collections of both data-entry surfaces with closed-list enforcement so free text was impossible. BR-013 records that this was 'an application-enforced enumeration only: the Gender column is plain TEXT with no database check constraint, so any value could be written by another client', that the enumeration was duplicated across two files, and that it 'disagrees with the dashboard, which counts only two of the three values'. The value set is carried forward unchanged; what is corrected is that it had no single home, no database constraint and no agreement with its one consumer. The data-domain assessment notes that gender describes a protected characteristic, so the value set is a policy artefact even though individual codes are not personal data.

requirements.description: The permitted programme values MUST be held as reference data with exactly one authoritative definition, each carrying a code, a display label, a nominal duration in years, an active flag and a sort position. Adding or retiring a programme MUST require no code change, no new query, no new presentation element and no rebuild. The initial value set MUST be exactly BCA, MCA and IIMCA.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Adding a programme is a data change only
acceptance_criteria.given: A new programme 'BSc' added to the reference data with a nominal duration
acceptance_criteria.when: The entry surface, the list filters and the statistics dashboard are read
acceptance_criteria.then: 'BSc' is selectable, filterable and counted, with no code change and no redeployment

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Retiring a programme preserves existing records
acceptance_criteria.given: An existing record enrolled on a programme that is then deactivated
acceptance_criteria.when: The record is opened for amendment
acceptance_criteria.then: It remains amendable and the deactivated programme is displayed and preserved per REQ-013

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered system
acceptance_criteria.then: Exactly one definition exists, against a legacy baseline of at least eight scattered declarations

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy taxonomy is carried forward unchanged in content. BR-014 records that it 'lives in at least eight places: two Items collections, two dead AutoCompleteCustomSource collections, three SQL literals and the tile labels', with no database constraint, no lookup table and no grouping, so 'adding a programme requires coordinated edits in every one of those places' and a record carrying any other value was counted nowhere. The decomposition strategy independently prescribes this same resolution, identifying the normalization of gender, programme and admission year into reference tables with real constraints as 'the one place the target schema legitimately gains relations the legacy single-table shape has none of'. The nominal-duration attribute is new and is what allows REQ-043 to derive the cohort count rather than assert five.

requirements.description: Admission year MUST be stored in a numeric type and the selectable set MUST be held as reference data derived at runtime. The set MUST always include the current academic year without a code change, and MUST impose no upper bound requiring a rebuild to extend. The field MUST be labelled consistently with the concept it holds.

acceptance_criteria.given: Any calendar year, including one later than any year present in the initial reference data
acceptance_criteria.then: The current academic year is selectable and a record can be created against it, where the legacy system could not record any intake after 2023

acceptance_criteria.given: A persisted admission year
acceptance_criteria.then: It is numeric, not text, and range and grouping predicates over it evaluate arithmetically

acceptance_criteria.given: The admission-year input and every report referring to it
acceptance_criteria.then: All use one term naming admission year; none is labelled 'Session', which denotes a different concept and is a retired column name from a superseded schema generation

acceptance_criteria.given: A new year added to the reference data
acceptance_criteria.then: The new year is selectable with no code change

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy set was five string literals from 2019 to 2023, declared in four Designer locations with closed-list enforcement. BR-015 rates it critical as 'a hard functional ceiling — the application cannot record a current intake': as of the Discovery date no student admitted after 2023 could be recorded through any application path, and because of BR-033 any record carrying a later year, however created, became permanently un-amendable. The column was text, so IM-009 records that cohort matching was lexical rather than arithmetic, meaning 'a whitespace-padded or non-canonical stored year is counted nowhere while being indistinguishable in the grid' — and that no range predicate would behave arithmetically either, 'which is likely why five equality queries were written instead of one grouped query'. Junk values 'A' and 'B' are already present in deleted rows recovered from page slack. The naming clause resolves ANOM-043: the field was labelled 'Session' on both entry surfaces while the column was named yoa and held a single year rather than a range.

requirements.description: The system MUST report the distribution of students by gender, derived by grouping over the data rather than from a compiled list of expected values, MUST include a bucket for values outside the active reference set, and MUST report a grand total against which the buckets reconcile. A visible discrepancy MUST be surfaced if the buckets do not sum to the total.

acceptance_criteria.given: 10 Active records: 5 'Male', 4 'Female', 1 'Other'
acceptance_criteria.then: It reports Male 5, Female 4 and Other 1, and a grand total of 10, where the legacy dashboard reported only Male and Female and counted the third nowhere

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Out-of-set values are visible, not lost
acceptance_criteria.given: A migrated record whose gender value is absent from the active reference set
acceptance_criteria.then: That record appears in an explicit other-or-unrecognised bucket and the grand total includes it

acceptance_criteria.given: Any breakdown
acceptance_criteria.then: They equal the reported grand total, and if they do not the system surfaces a visible discrepancy rather than displaying an unreconciled set

acceptance_criteria.given: The gender breakdown
acceptance_criteria.then: One grouped aggregation query is issued, not one per expected value

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy dashboard ran exactly two count queries, for Male and for Female, while the entry surfaces permitted three values. BR-070 records that a student recorded as the third 'is storable, listable and editable but is counted in no gender statistic and in no total, so the two gender tiles do not sum to the student population and there is no tile, label or total anywhere on the dashboard that would reveal the shortfall'. The absence of a reconciling total is the specific mechanism by which three independent undercounts — gender, programme and cohort — remained invisible, which is why prescribing the total is as load-bearing here as prescribing the grouping. An empty or null gender was likewise counted nowhere.

requirements.description: The system MUST report the distribution of students by programme, derived by grouping over the data against the active programme reference set, MUST include a bucket for values outside that set, and MUST reconcile to the grand total. Adding a programme MUST require no change to the statistics computation or presentation.

acceptance_criteria.given: A new programme added to the reference data and three records enrolled on it
acceptance_criteria.then: The new programme appears with a count of 3 and the grand total includes those records, with no code change

acceptance_criteria.given: A record whose programme value is absent from the active set
acceptance_criteria.then: It appears in an explicit unrecognised bucket rather than being silently excluded

acceptance_criteria.given: The programme breakdown
acceptance_criteria.then: One grouped aggregation query is issued, against a legacy baseline of one per programme

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy programme distribution was three separate count queries whose values were literals in the dashboard source, matching three literal tile captions and the three-value selector lists. BR-071 records that there was 'no GROUP BY and no data-driven enumeration, so adding a programme requires a new query, a new tile, a new label and edits to both Designer combo lists', that 'a record carrying any other course value is counted nowhere', and that 'as with gender, no total exists that would expose the omission'. Two further programme tiles existed but were orphaned and permanently read zero, addressed under REQ-048.

requirements.description: Every derived temporal value MUST be computed from an injectable time source resolved at request time, never from a compiled constant. The academic-year boundary used to derive a cohort MUST be supplied by configuration rather than assumed to be the calendar year.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Time source is injectable and effective
acceptance_criteria.given: A test substituting a fixed current date of 2027-03-01
acceptance_criteria.then: Every cohort classification reflects 2027, proving no compiled temporal constant remains

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cohorts are correct in any calendar year
acceptance_criteria.given: A record with admission year 2024 and a current date in the 2026-27 academic year
acceptance_criteria.then: It is reported as a third-year cohort member, not as a first-year

acceptance_criteria.given: A configured academic-year boundary other than 1 January
acceptance_criteria.when: A date either side of that boundary is used as the current date
acceptance_criteria.then: Cohort assignment changes at the configured boundary, not at the calendar-year boundary

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy dashboard assigned a local variable the literal value 2023 and computed its five cohort buckets as that value minus zero through four, never reading the system clock. BR-072 records that it was therefore 'frozen in the 2023-24 academic year' and that as of the Discovery date it 'mislabels every cohort by three years, reporting students admitted in 2023 as first-years when they are fourth-years'. Correcting it required a source change and a rebuild; changing the workstation clock had no effect, so the staleness could not even be worked around operationally. BR-072 is rated high complexity precisely because 'a single magic constant silently invalidates five of the dashboard's twelve statistics' and 'whose wrongness grows by one cohort per year with no failure signal'. The quality-risk assessment dates the incorrect output from 1 January 2024. The academic-year boundary requires SME confirmation: no artefact states it, and it determines cohort assignment for every record.

requirements.description: The system MUST report the distribution of students by cohort, with the number of cohort buckets DERIVED from the nominal durations held in the programme reference data rather than asserted as a constant. It MUST include a residual bucket for admissions outside the derived window, MUST reconcile to the grand total, and MUST label each cohort distinctly in text.

acceptance_criteria.given: Programme reference data whose longest nominal duration is three years
acceptance_criteria.then: Three cohort buckets are reported plus a residual bucket, not five, and changing the longest duration changes the bucket count with no code change

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Older admissions are visible, not silently dropped
acceptance_criteria.given: A record whose admission year precedes the derived window
acceptance_criteria.then: It appears in the residual bucket and the grand total includes it, where the legacy system counted it nowhere with no bucket to reveal the omission

acceptance_criteria.given: The rendered cohort figures
acceptance_criteria.when: They are read by a screen reader with no access to images or colour
acceptance_criteria.then: Each is identified by distinct text naming its cohort, satisfying REQ-102

acceptance_criteria.given: The cohort breakdown
acceptance_criteria.then: One grouped aggregation query is issued, against a legacy baseline of five

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy dashboard hardcoded five cohort buckets — five queries, five counters, five tiles, five labels. BR-073 records that 'five is not derived from the programme catalogue: the three recognised programmes are three-year and two-year degrees, so a fifth-year bucket has no clear referent', and that students admitted more than four years before the frozen current year were 'silently excluded from every year statistic' with 'no other or earlier bucket and no total against which the omission could be detected'. IM-002 adds that five is asserted in four places and justified nowhere. Deriving the count from nominal duration is what makes the figure explicable; the residual bucket is what makes any remaining exclusion visible. The distinct-labelling clause resolves accessibility finding A11Y-003 at serious severity: all five legacy tiles carried the identical caption with the ordinal carried solely by decorative coloured numeral images, so IM-033 records they were 'not distinguishable from their text, not localizable and not greppable'.

requirements.description: Admission year MUST be compared and grouped arithmetically as a number, never as a string literal concatenated into a query. Cohort aggregation MUST be expressed as a single grouped query per axis rather than one equality query per expected value.

acceptance_criteria.given: The cohort computation
acceptance_criteria.then: Admission year is compared numerically and bound as a parameter; no quoted string literal is concatenated

acceptance_criteria.given: A migrated record whose source admission year was stored as text with trailing whitespace
acceptance_criteria.then: It is either normalized to a number or quarantined; it cannot silently fail to match while appearing normal in the list

acceptance_criteria.given: A request for all records admitted in or after a given year
acceptance_criteria.then: The result is arithmetically correct, where the legacy text column made such a predicate unusable

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy cohort queries built their predicates by converting an integer year to a string and concatenating it into a quoted literal to match a text column. BR-074 records that 'comparison is therefore lexical, not arithmetic: a stored value of 2023 with trailing whitespace, or any non-canonical representation, fails to match while being indistinguishable in the grid'. It further records this as 'the only remaining place in the application where SQL is assembled by concatenation outside the search path, though it is not injectable because the concatenated value is an Integer' — and REQ-022 nonetheless forbids it, because that safety is incidental rather than guaranteed. IM-009 identifies the lexical comparison as the likely reason five equality queries were written instead of one grouped query, so typing the attribute numerically is the precondition for the optimization.

requirements.description: Every reported statistic MUST state its population scope explicitly — which lifecycle states are included and which excluded — and MUST state the as-of instant at which it was computed. The system MUST be capable of reporting the active population and the all-time population as distinct figures.

acceptance_criteria.given: Any reported figure
acceptance_criteria.then: It states which lifecycle states it includes, so that an active-population figure cannot be mistaken for an all-time figure

acceptance_criteria.given: Any reported figure
acceptance_criteria.then: It carries the instant at which it was computed

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Active and all-time are both obtainable and differ
acceptance_criteria.given: A datastore with 10 Active and 3 Archived records
acceptance_criteria.then: The active figure is 10 and the all-time figure is 13, and the two are separately labelled

requirements.anomaly_details: BR-075 is an undocumented definition rather than a defect: every legacy count queried the whole table with no scoping predicate beyond the single attribute it broke down by — no academic-year scope, no active-versus-graduated status, no enrolment state and no date filter — because the schema had no status column to filter on. The consequence it records is decisive: 'because deletion is physical, a student who leaves is removed rather than marked inactive, so all-time and currently enrolled are the same number by construction and the dashboard cannot distinguish them'. Once REQ-027 introduces logical deletion and REQ-090 introduces lifecycle state, the two populations genuinely diverge, so the scope must be stated rather than inherited. BR-075 also records that 'no dashboard statistic reports a grand total, so no cross-check between the three axes is possible'. Which lifecycle states constitute the reportable active population requires SME confirmation.

requirements.description: A statistic that could not be computed MUST be rendered as explicitly unavailable and MUST NOT display a numeric value. The system MUST distinguish a measured zero from an uncomputed value in both its interface and its data contract. Failure to compute one statistic MUST NOT prevent the others from being presented and MUST NOT terminate the application.

acceptance_criteria.given: A datastore with no records, and separately a datastore that cannot be reached
acceptance_criteria.when: The dashboard is rendered in each case
acceptance_criteria.then: The first shows zeros marked as measured, the second shows every figure marked unavailable; the two presentations are visibly and programmatically different

acceptance_criteria.given: A computation in which one axis fails and two succeed
acceptance_criteria.then: The two successful axes display their figures, the failed axis is marked unavailable, and the application continues running

acceptance_criteria.given: An unreachable datastore at startup
acceptance_criteria.then: It starts, reports the datastore as unreachable per REQ-082, and does not crash before a usable surface is presented

requirements.anomaly_details: All ten legacy count controls carried a baked default text of '0', and the statistics loader had no exception handling anywhere and ran from the form load handler. BR-076 records both halves of the consequence: a provider failure, a missing datastore file or a connection closed by a prior deletion 'produces an unhandled exception that terminates the application at startup', while any partial failure that did survive 'would leave tiles reading a plausible 0 rather than blank or an error'. The summary is exact: 'a genuinely empty table and a total failure both display twelve zeros'. A default that disguises failure as data is the mechanism by which the three undercounts in REQ-040, REQ-041 and REQ-043 stayed invisible. IM-022 adds that the controls were labels despite names implying text boxes, addressed under ANOM-044.

requirements.description: No reporting capability is derived from the legacy Project Report control, which is OMITTED. Should a reporting capability be required, it MUST be specified from stated stakeholder requirements, MUST serve any document it offers from a location the deploying organisation controls, MUST NOT embed an external repository URL, and MUST handle the failure of any external process it launches.

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered system
acceptance_criteria.when: It is scanned for external host addresses
acceptance_criteria.then: No third-party repository URL is present, and no feature depends on a third-party repository remaining public at a fixed path

acceptance_criteria.given: Any feature that launches an external process or handler
acceptance_criteria.when: No handler is registered or the launch fails
acceptance_criteria.then: The failure is reported to the principal and the application continues running

requirements.anomaly_details: OMISSION WITH JUSTIFICATION, recorded because stakeholders will ask. The legacy Project Report control did not open the report committed in the repository; it launched the default browser against a hardcoded absolute GitHub URL pointing at that same file in the author's public repository, with a source comment still reading 'Replace with your desired web link'. It implemented no reporting logic whatsoever: the interface inventory classifies it as kind 'unknown' on the explicit grounds that 'it is neither a report the application produces nor an api/file-exchange integration' and states that 'any real reporting capability is unimplemented'; the capability catalogue independently calls it 'a dead link to an external PDF'. BR-080 records that it required internet access, depended on a third party, leaked the fact of use to an external host, and crashed the application unhandled on a machine with no registered URL handler — while 'the identical PDF exists locally in the repository root and is never used'. SME confirmation is required precisely so this omission is not mistaken for a decision that reporting is unnecessary: stakeholders may expect a feature that has never existed.

requirements.description: The dashboard MUST present exactly one presentation element per statistic it reports, MUST NOT contain any element that no computation writes to, and MUST NOT conceal an element by positioning it outside its container's bounds. Elements not intended to be presented MUST be removed.

acceptance_criteria.given: The rendered dashboard
acceptance_criteria.when: Each presentation element is traced to the computation that populates it
acceptance_criteria.then: Every element has exactly one writer and every statistic has exactly one element

acceptance_criteria.given: The dashboard at any window size, including resized
acceptance_criteria.then: No element is positioned outside its parent's bounds, and resizing exposes nothing previously hidden

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Nothing unintended in the focus order
acceptance_criteria.given: The dashboard
acceptance_criteria.when: A principal traverses it by keyboard alone
acceptance_criteria.then: Focus visits only elements intended to be presented, in the order of REQ-103

requirements.anomaly_details: OMISSION WITH JUSTIFICATION. The legacy dashboard contained two duplicate statistic tiles — a second BCA tile and a second IIMCA tile, each with its own count label — that the statistics loader never wrote to, so they displayed their baked default of '0' forever. They were nested in the wrong parent and pushed outside its bounds by coordinates of minus 373 and plus 373 within a 343-pixel-wide parent 'rather than being hidden or deleted — so any change to the parent's size, or a move to a layout container, would expose two tiles that are structurally incapable of being correct'. No requirement is generated for them because they produce no behaviour a stakeholder could depend on. They are not merely unused but actively harmful: accessibility finding A11Y-005 records that they remain in the control collection and the focus order, so a keyboard or screen-reader user can land on them out of sequence, and that one of them overlaps a real tile. SME confirmation is sought only to record that no stakeholder expected a second figure for either programme, since the duplication is unexplained.

requirements.description: Each unit of work MUST acquire its own datastore connection, use it within an explicit scope, and release it deterministically on completion whether successful or not. No connection may be shared across operations or surfaces. Connection lifecycle MUST NOT depend on implicit framework behaviour, and a connection in an unusable state MUST be discarded and replaced rather than reused.

acceptance_criteria.given: Any operation requiring datastore access
acceptance_criteria.then: Its connection is released, and no connection remains open after the operation returns

acceptance_criteria.criterion: One operation's failure does not affect the next
acceptance_criteria.given: An operation that fails mid-read
acceptance_criteria.when: An unrelated operation is performed immediately afterwards
acceptance_criteria.then: It succeeds normally; no resource left by the failed operation degrades it

acceptance_criteria.given: A connection that has entered an unusable state
acceptance_criteria.when: The next unit of work runs
acceptance_criteria.then: A new connection is acquired; the unusable one is not reused and no silent state check masks it

acceptance_criteria.given: The data-access implementation
acceptance_criteria.then: No path relies on a framework helper to open or close a connection implicitly

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy application opened exactly one shared connection held in a module-level public variable, opened lazily by whichever surface asked first and reused by all others, with no pool, no per-operation connection, no deterministic-release construct and no close on exit. BR-003 records that because child surfaces were hosted simultaneously and only hidden rather than disposed, two could hold live readers against the one connection, and the provider permits only one open reader — so an unclosed reader blocked every other operation.
