The structural assessment rates this coupling critical and states 'every decomposition boundary below must cut this edge', noting the module has the highest fan-in of any code node while holding zero SQL: 'a shared mutable resource, not a service'. The unusable-state clause corrects BR-001's recorded boundary condition that a broken or connecting state is tested by neither branch, 'so the connection is left unusable'. The implicit-lifecycle clause matters because the legacy adapter's auto-open behaviour masked the BR-004 defect at the one call site that would have revealed it.

requirements.description: The datastore location and all connection parameters MUST be supplied by external configuration resolved at startup. No absolute filesystem path, credential or endpoint address may appear in source or in a compiled artefact, and the same build artefact MUST operate against different environments by configuration alone.

acceptance_criteria.given: One build artefact and two environments with different datastore configuration
acceptance_criteria.then: It connects correctly in both with no rebuild and no source change

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered source and build output
acceptance_criteria.then: No absolute filesystem path, credential or endpoint address is present, against a legacy baseline of two hardcoded absolute paths and one hardcoded external URL

acceptance_criteria.given: A fresh clone and the documented configuration values
acceptance_criteria.when: The application is built and started
acceptance_criteria.then: It connects to its configured datastore, where a legacy clean clone could not connect to its own bundled database without a source change

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy connection string embedded the original developer's absolute workstation path on a drive D: with no configuration entry, no relative path and no environment override; the application's config file contained only a runtime declaration and no connection-string section. BR-002 records the decisive consequence: 'the database file committed to the repository is therefore NOT the file the application opens: on any machine other than the author's, the application fails at startup', and 'the repository-committed studentDB.accdb is never read by the running application — an orphan datastore'. db-archaeology corroborates with the triply nested path and the committed lock file recording the capture machine and user. A configuration mechanism did exist — a generated accessor over an empty settings store — and was entirely unused, which ANOM-050 omits as dead code and which explains how the hardcoding was possible. The decomposition strategy records externalizing configuration as 'a prerequisite for every other boundary'.

requirements.description: No datastore connection or other mutable resource may be shared between presentation surfaces or between concurrent operations. Each operation MUST be isolated such that its resource state cannot affect any other.

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered codebase
acceptance_criteria.when: It is scanned for module-level or globally reachable mutable resources
acceptance_criteria.then: None is found, against a legacy baseline of one shared global mutable connection reached by four surfaces

acceptance_criteria.given: Two operations executing concurrently
acceptance_criteria.then: The other proceeds unaffected and does not fail for want of an available reader

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy connection was a public module-level variable, so all four surfaces issued commands against the same physical connection object. BR-003 records that this 'creates implicit cross-module temporal coupling between four form modules that are otherwise independent' and that its failure mode was concrete: an exception thrown before the reader was closed left it open and 'poisoning the connection for every later operation until the process restarts'.

requirements.description: No component may close, dispose or otherwise invalidate a resource it did not acquire. A component MUST NOT leave shared or ambient state altered in a way that affects a later operation performed by a different component.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Archive does not break a later dashboard read
acceptance_criteria.given: A principal who has just archived a record
acceptance_criteria.when: They immediately navigate to the statistics dashboard
acceptance_criteria.then: The dashboard renders successfully with correct figures, where the legacy sequence raised an unhandled fault and terminated the application

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered codebase
acceptance_criteria.then: Every release is performed by the component that acquired the resource

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy delete path contained the application's only connection close, leaving the shared connection closed with no paired reopen. BR-004 traces the consequence across three modules: the list's own reload survived because the data adapter opens and closes implicitly, 'masking the defect at the one call site that would have revealed it', while the dashboard loader issued a scalar query without reopening and so 'navigating Home after a delete raises InvalidOperationException inside a method that has no exception handling at all'. The call graph singles this out as 'the only edge in the graph that tears down shared global state another module owns'. BR-004 also records a second, subtler symptom: deleting then creating a record produced a misleading error message after the new row had already been inserted. The shortest reproduction is delete followed by Dashboard.

requirements.description: Parameter binding MUST be by name, and an automated test MUST assert that each attribute reaches its intended column. The system MUST NOT depend on the textual ordering of a parameter collection for correctness, and the attribute-to-column mapping MUST be declared in exactly one place per entity.

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered data access
acceptance_criteria.then: Parameters are resolved by name and reordering the declaration does not change which column each value reaches

acceptance_criteria.given: A record with a distinct recognisable value in every attribute
acceptance_criteria.then: Every value returns in its own attribute, and the test fails if any two same-typed attributes are transposed

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered codebase
acceptance_criteria.then: Exactly one exists per entity, against a legacy baseline duplicating the mapping between the create and amend paths

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy provider did not support named parameters: the name tokens in the query text were anonymous placeholders and values were consumed strictly in the order added. BR-018 records that the four parameterized statements 'currently work only because the AddWithValue calls happen to appear in the same order as the placeholders. The names are decorative, so any future reordering of either the SQL column list or the AddWithValue block silently shifts every value one column sideways rather than raising an error.' The worst case is explicit: first and last name, and the two telephone numbers, are same-typed adjacent pairs, so 'a transposition between them would corrupt data silently with no exception at all'. The source's own appearance of name-based binding contradicted the provider's actual semantics, so a developer reading the legacy code would draw the wrong conclusion about what was safe to change — which is why this is prescribed explicitly rather than assumed.

requirements.description: Every conversion between a presentation value and a stored value MUST be explicit and MUST declare its failure behaviour. The system MUST NOT rely on implicit type coercion, implicit narrowing conversion or late binding for data access or reference-value handling.

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered codebase
acceptance_criteria.when: Conversions between presentation and stored values are traced
acceptance_criteria.then: Each is explicit and names its failure behaviour; none relies on the runtime or the datastore provider to infer a type

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Type errors surface at build time
acceptance_criteria.given: A change introducing a narrowing conversion or a late-bound member access
acceptance_criteria.then: The build fails, where the legacy build accepted it and failed only at runtime

acceptance_criteria.given: Any bound parameter
acceptance_criteria.then: Its type is stated explicitly rather than inferred from the supplied value

traces_to.source_file: Flat Design/Student Management System Siddharth Jain.vbproj

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy project compiled with strict type checking off, permitting late binding and implicit narrowing throughout the hand-written code. BR-091 records that this is the enabling precondition for at least five distinct runtime-only failure modes across four modules: the two unguarded reference-selector dereferences, the untyped parameter coercion behind the telephone ceiling, and both halves of the date-of-birth string confusion. It states that 'several of the application's most significant data-integrity rules exist only because this switch is off' and that turning it on 'would surface these defects as compile errors, which is the recommended first step of any port'. The generated files set strict checking on locally, so the weak setting applied only to code a human wrote. The data-flow trace independently records the provider inferring parameter types from supplied values as an implicit encode transformation on every personal-data flow.

requirements.description: For each comparison the system performs it MUST define whether that comparison is case-sensitive, and MUST apply the same semantics whether the comparison is evaluated in application code or in the datastore. Roll-number uniqueness and lookup, and reference-value matching, MUST be case-insensitive.

acceptance_criteria.given: A comparison of two values differing only in letter case
acceptance_criteria.when: It is evaluated in application code and in the datastore
acceptance_criteria.then: Both return the same result

acceptance_criteria.given: A record whose stored gender code is 'male' in lower case
acceptance_criteria.then: It matches the active value 'Male' and is presented as selected, where the legacy exact case-sensitive lookup left the selector blank and made the record un-amendable

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Key comparison is case-insensitive and consistent
acceptance_criteria.given: Roll numbers differing only in case
acceptance_criteria.when: Uniqueness is checked and lookups are performed
acceptance_criteria.then: They are treated as the same key by both the constraint and every query, removing the legacy divergence

traces_to.source_file: Flat Design/Student Management System Siddharth Jain.vbproj

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy project set binary string comparison, making application-code comparison case-sensitive and ordinal, while the datastore engine compared text case-insensitively. BR-092 records that 'the same conceptual equality therefore has two different answers depending on which layer evaluates it': the amendment selector rebinding failed on a case difference while the dashboard counts and the search's roll-number equality ignored case. Its warning is directly aimed at this programme of work — 'any logic moved between the two layers during modernization changes behaviour' — which is precisely what a replatform does, so leaving the semantics implicit would guarantee a behavioural regression. BR-092 also identifies the one configuration in which BR-037's multi-row mutation becomes reachable: roll numbers differing only in case are distinct to the case-sensitive index but equal to the case-insensitive predicate. RISK-05 flags the related casing divergence as breaking on a case-sensitive target engine.

requirements.description: Every operation performing more than one write, or a write plus a dependent state change, MUST execute inside a single transaction that commits atomically or rolls back entirely. The system MUST NOT report an operation as failed when its data change has committed, nor as succeeded when it has not. Transaction scope MUST be owned by the service layer and MUST NOT be inferred from connection state.

acceptance_criteria.given: A create whose audit write will fail
acceptance_criteria.then: Neither the record nor the audit entry persists, and the principal is told the operation failed

acceptance_criteria.given: An operation whose post-commit notification work fails
acceptance_criteria.then: The principal is told the operation succeeded, because it did; the notification failure is logged separately and does not present as a save failure

acceptance_criteria.given: A create spanning the student, its contact points, its guardian reference and its enrolment
acceptance_criteria.when: Any one of those writes fails
acceptance_criteria.then: None of them persists

acceptance_criteria.given: The service layer
acceptance_criteria.then: Each is opened and closed explicitly by the service layer, not implied by a connection's lifetime

requirements.anomaly_details: No legacy code path began, committed or rolled back a transaction. BR-093 records that every mutation was a single autocommitted statement, 'sufficient for the current single-statement operations but means there is no atomicity between a mutation and its dependent side effects'. Two concrete consequences follow: the create path committed a row and then performed refresh work that could itself fail, so BR-022 records that 'the user is told the save failed when it did not'; and a delete-and-recreate re-key 'loses the record irrecoverably if interrupted in between'. BR-093's forward-looking note is the operative one for this SRS — 'any future multi-table operation would have no consistency mechanism to build on' — because the prescribed data model adds exactly such writes through reference tables, contact points, guardian references and audit entries.

requirements.description: The system MUST implement optimistic concurrency control over student records: the version token read with a record MUST be submitted with any amendment, and an amendment whose token does not match the stored value MUST be rejected with a conflict error identifying the attributes changed by the other party.

acceptance_criteria.given: Two principals who both retrieved the same record at version 4, the first having saved a change to the programme so the stored version is 5
acceptance_criteria.when: The second submits an amendment at version 4
acceptance_criteria.then: It is rejected, the error states that the record changed and names programme as the attribute the other party changed, and the stored record is unaffected

acceptance_criteria.given: Any conflicting pair of amendments
acceptance_criteria.then: The second is rejected rather than applied; neither party's change is silently discarded

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Version advances on persisted change only
acceptance_criteria.given: An amendment that changes no attribute
acceptance_criteria.then: The version does not advance

requirements.anomaly_details: Single-instance mode was explicitly disabled, so any number of copies could run against the same datastore file, each with its own shared connection. BR-094 records that there was 'no optimistic concurrency token, no row version, no timestamp and no change detection: the update writes all nine fields unconditionally, so the last save wins silently and the loser's edits are destroyed with no warning to either user'. Refresh was navigation-driven only, so each instance showed arbitrarily stale data. File-level locking serialised writes but 'provides no application-level conflict detection'. BR-094 notes the defect has probably never been observed because the hardcoded local path made genuine multi-user use unlikely — which makes it a latent hazard that a replatform to a shared server datastore would activate immediately. The conflict-resolution experience requires SME confirmation.

requirements.description: Every student record MUST carry a system-generated, immutable surrogate identifier that is never user-supplied, never reused and never presented as the business identifier. All internal references and all mutations MUST address records by that identifier.

acceptance_criteria.given: A create request that includes a value purporting to be a record identifier
acceptance_criteria.then: The supplied value is ignored and the system generates the identifier

acceptance_criteria.given: Any amendment, archive or purge
acceptance_criteria.then: It addresses the surrogate identifier, not the roll number

acceptance_criteria.given: A purged record
acceptance_criteria.then: It does not receive the purged record's identifier

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy system had no surrogate key: db-archaeology records that 'an ID column does not occur in the file at all'. Roll number served as the key for every single-row read, amendment and deletion, and the list read it back by attribute name to drive those operations. Its enforcement rested entirely on one index whose existence two Discovery passes disagreed about, and which permitted the empty string. db-archaeology's own remediation prescribes exactly this shape: an integer surrogate key with roll number as a separately constrained unique business key. Decoupling identity from the business key is also what makes REQ-011's atomic roll-number correction possible, since the record's identity no longer changes when its roll number does.

requirements.description: Telephone contact points MUST be modelled so that each carries an explicit type or purpose and so that their number is not fixed by the schema. The system MUST NOT distinguish contact points by position alone.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Contact points carry an explicit type
acceptance_criteria.given: A record with two telephone numbers
acceptance_criteria.then: Each carries a declared type, and neither is identified merely as the first or second slot

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cardinality is not fixed at two
acceptance_criteria.given: The data model
acceptance_criteria.then: Adding a third contact point requires no schema change

acceptance_criteria.given: An attempt to mark two contact points as primary for one student
acceptance_criteria.then: It is rejected

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy model held two telephone attributes distinguished only by an 'alternate' qualifier in the second's name. The data-domain assessment identifies them as a distinct logical entity precisely on this basis, describing them as 'two unlabelled telephone slots denormalised into the student row' whose cardinality in the legacy system is 'exactly two, positionally distinguished only; there is no contact-type, no preference order and no validity window'. The rename is what makes REQ-005's widening meaningful: widening the column without naming what each slot means would preserve the ambiguity.

requirements.description: The system MUST reject a date of birth that is in the future or that implies an age outside a configured plausible range, and MUST report such a rejection as a validation error naming date of birth and stating the permitted range.

acceptance_criteria.given: A submission whose date of birth is tomorrow
acceptance_criteria.then: It is rejected naming date of birth, and no record is created

acceptance_criteria.given: A configured plausible range and a submission implying an age far outside it
acceptance_criteria.then: It is rejected naming date of birth and stating the permitted range

acceptance_criteria.given: A submission implying an age inside the configured range
acceptance_criteria.then: It is accepted

acceptance_criteria.given: A changed plausible range in configuration
acceptance_criteria.when: A submission at the old boundary is retried
acceptance_criteria.then: Acceptance follows the new range with no code change

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy system applied no plausibility check whatsoever: BR-021 records that 'future birth dates and eighteenth-century birth dates are both accepted' and that the control's full default range of 1753-01-01 to 9998-12-31 was selectable and storable. Its most telling boundary condition is evidence that no such rule ever existed: 'the existing two live rows carry a 2009 date of birth against a 2019 year of admission, implying a nine-year-old admitted student'. db-archaeology independently describes both live rows as implausible test data. The plausible range is a business parameter no artefact supplies and requires SME confirmation, which is why it is configured rather than fixed here.

requirements.description: Before any target schema is generated, the real column types, nullability, defaults, collation and index definitions of the legacy datastore MUST be read from a live database engine, and the prescribed data model MUST be reconciled against them. Migration MUST read only the ten live attributes, MUST validate every migrated value against the prescribed constraints, and MUST quarantine rather than silently coerce any value that fails.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Live schema is read before DDL
acceptance_criteria.given: The migration programme
acceptance_criteria.then: It is blocked until a live-engine schema read has been recorded and reconciled against srs-data-model.json, resolving the open RISK-03 and DS-RISK-02

acceptance_criteria.given: A legacy datastore retaining superseded table-definition generations
acceptance_criteria.then: It reads only the ten live attributes and asserts that no source record carries data in a retired attribute

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Invalid values are quarantined, not coerced
acceptance_criteria.given: Source records carrying out-of-vocabulary values such as a programme of '2' or an admission year of 'A'
acceptance_criteria.then: They are quarantined with a reportable reason and are not silently mapped to a valid value

acceptance_criteria.given: The prescribed attribute set
acceptance_criteria.then: Every attribute derived from a legacy column records that column's name, so the rename is fully traceable

traces_to.line_note: Binary artefact; every type statement in Discovery derives from reading the file as bytes, never from an engine.

requirements.anomaly_details: This requirement exists because the single largest gap in the Discovery record is the one that bounds the entire data model. No pass ever had a live engine: 'every statement about the .accdb's internals comes from reading the file as bytes, never from opening it through a database engine'. The structural pass declared column types, nullability, primary key and indexes UNKNOWN and declined to guess; db-archaeology reported concrete declared types; the data-domain pass arbitrated in favour of db-archaeology, and that arbitration is what srs-data-model.json carries. One conflict remains unresolved by design — the telephone columns are reported as integer by one pass and as text by another, which the data-domain pass rules is itself the defect. DS-RISK-02 is recorded as blocking target-schema generation and RISK-03 as blocking decisive cutover. The decomposition strategy's first target prescription is adopted verbatim in effect: read real types from a live engine before writing DDL. The quarantine clause is grounded in measured evidence that the validation gap was exercised: deleted rows recovered from page slack carry programme values of '2' and '3' and admission-year values of 'A' and 'B'.

requirements.description: The system SHOULD allow an authorized administrator to add a reference value, amend its display label and sort position, and deactivate it, without a code change or redeployment. Deactivating a value in use MUST NOT delete it and MUST NOT render any existing record un-amendable.

acceptance_criteria.given: An authorized administrator
acceptance_criteria.when: They add a new programme with a display label and nominal duration
acceptance_criteria.then: It becomes selectable, filterable and countable with no code change and no redeployment

acceptance_criteria.given: A reference value in use by existing records
acceptance_criteria.then: It is no longer offered for new records, existing records retain it, and those records remain amendable per REQ-013

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Deletion of an in-use value is refused
acceptance_criteria.given: A reference value in use
acceptance_criteria.when: The administrator attempts to delete it
acceptance_criteria.then: The attempt is refused and deactivation is offered instead

acceptance_criteria.given: Any reference-data change
acceptance_criteria.then: An audit entry records the acting principal, the instant and the prior and new values

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy system had no reference-data management of any kind. The data-domain assessment records that domain D3 'owns no physical columns' and that its physical system of record is 'none' — the vocabularies existed only as compiled literals, which is why BR-014 records that adding a programme 'requires coordinated edits in every one of those places' across at least eight locations. The deactivation clause is what prevents this requirement from reintroducing BR-033: if a value could be deleted outright, every record holding it would become un-amendable, which is the exact legacy failure. Priority is should rather than must because Discovery evidences the structural need but no stakeholder requirement for a self-service administration surface; the underlying data-driven vocabulary in REQ-030 through REQ-032 is must-strength regardless.

requirements.description: The system MUST authenticate the principal before rendering any surface that displays or accepts student data. It MUST NOT accept possession of an operating-system session as an authentication event, and MUST NOT read or write student data on behalf of an unauthenticated principal under any circumstance.

acceptance_criteria.given: An unauthenticated principal who can launch the client
acceptance_criteria.then: Only an authentication surface is presented; no student record, statistic or record count is displayed

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal with an active interactive desktop session on the host
acceptance_criteria.then: Authentication is still required

acceptance_criteria.given: An unauthenticated caller
acceptance_criteria.when: They invoke any student-data service operation directly
acceptance_criteria.then: It is denied before any datastore access occurs, and the denial is audited per REQ-063

requirements.anomaly_details: PRESCRIBED FROM A NAMED ABSENCE, which is this requirement's evidence. BR-090 records that the legacy application had 'no login, no user identity, no roles, no permissions and no audit of actor'; the framework's authentication mode was set to Windows but 'that only governs the My.User object, which the code never reads: no code path anywhere tests identity, group membership or privilege'. The identity assessment states it most precisely: 'There is not merely no second factor; there is no first factor at the application boundary.' The dashboard opened directly with full privilege and the load handler opened the datastore and rendered figures with no gate preceding it. BR-090 is explicit about why the absence must be recorded as a requirement rather than skipped: 'a modernization target that assumes authorization exists somewhere in this code will find nothing to port'.

requirements.description: The system MUST enforce an explicit authorization decision on every create, read, amend, archive, purge, erase and reference-data operation, evaluated against the authenticated principal's permissions on the server side of the trust boundary.

acceptance_criteria.given: The operation set of the delivered system
acceptance_criteria.when: Each is invoked by a principal lacking permission for it
acceptance_criteria.then: Each is denied, and no operation exists that performs student-data access without an authorization check

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal without read permission
acceptance_criteria.when: They request the record list or the statistics dashboard
acceptance_criteria.then: The request is denied; read is not treated as unprivileged

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Client state is not the control
acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered client
acceptance_criteria.then: No operation's authorization depends on a control's enabled, visible or read-only state

requirements.anomaly_details: PRESCRIBED FROM A NAMED ABSENCE. BR-090 records that 'every create, read, update and delete path executes without any privilege test' and that 'anyone able to launch the executable and reach the Access file has unrestricted create, read, update and delete authority over every student record'. The structural assessment corroborates with 'there is no user concept, no roles and no audit column on the table: every operator has unrestricted create/read/update/delete over all student records, including the PII fields'. The only legacy gate in front of a destructive operation was the row-selection test, which BR-055 itself calls 'the closest thing the application has to an authorization check' — a role REQ-025 now returns to selection validity alone.

requirements.description: Authorization MUST deny by default: an operation for which no explicit grant exists MUST be refused. Adding a new operation MUST NOT make it reachable until a grant is defined for it.

acceptance_criteria.given: A newly added operation with no permission grant defined
acceptance_criteria.then: It is denied, and the absence of a grant is reported as a configuration defect

acceptance_criteria.given: An authenticated principal with no permissions assigned
acceptance_criteria.then: Every one is denied; authentication alone confers nothing

requirements.anomaly_details: Deny-by-default is prescribed because the legacy posture was the exact inverse — grant-by-default with no check anywhere — and because the actor model in srs.json records only ONE evidenced user class. With no role differentiation yet confirmed by a stakeholder, a permissive default would silently grant every future principal full authority over personal data, reproducing the legacy posture under a new name. BR-090's test hint makes the legacy default explicit: 'Launching the executable grants immediate full access — this is the designed behaviour' and 'None — there is no path that denies access.'

requirements.description: The system MUST record an audit entry for every authentication success, authentication failure, authorization denial, session establishment and session expiry, attributable to the principal or the attempted identity.

acceptance_criteria.given: A failed authentication attempt
acceptance_criteria.then: An audit entry with operation AuthenticationFailure records the attempted identity, the instant and the source, without recording the submitted credential

acceptance_criteria.given: An authorization denial
acceptance_criteria.then: An audit entry with operation AuthorizationDenial records the principal, the operation attempted and the instant

acceptance_criteria.given: The audit store after an authentication failure
acceptance_criteria.then: No password, token or other credential value is present

requirements.anomaly_details: PRESCRIBED FROM A NAMED ABSENCE. There was no actor to attribute anything to and no audit of any kind. The identity assessment records the consequence for attribution: the credential-less data path meant 'no per-user attribution of reads or writes is possible'. The data-flow assessment states it at critical severity: 'Any person who can launch the executable can read, alter or delete every personal record, and no record of who did so exists anywhere.'

requirements.description: The datastore MUST authenticate every connecting principal, and the authenticated end-user identity MUST be propagated to the data tier rather than replaced by a shared service identity. No access path to student data may exist that bypasses the application's authorization layer.

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal with host or network access to the datastore but no application authorization
acceptance_criteria.when: They attempt to read student data with a general-purpose database client
acceptance_criteria.then: Access is denied by the datastore itself

acceptance_criteria.given: An authenticated principal performing a read
acceptance_criteria.when: The datastore's own audit is inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: The operation is attributed to that principal, not to a shared application account

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No readable data file is distributed
acceptance_criteria.given: The deployment package and the repository
acceptance_criteria.then: Neither contains a datastore file holding student data

requirements.anomaly_details: This is the requirement that makes REQ-060 and REQ-061 non-bypassable, and the identity assessment is unusually direct about why it cannot be deferred: 'this path is reachable WITHOUT the application: any OLEDB client, or Microsoft Access itself, pointed at the same .accdb obtains the same full read/write access, so any authentication added to the WinForms client alone would be a bypassable control.' The interface inventory records the same file as 'an uncontrolled second access path to the data that bypasses the application entirely'. The assessment directs that this be sequenced 'BEFORE or WITH the ambient-Windows retirement, never after'. BR-090 adds the measured basis: no database password, Jet workgroup security unused, and the executable requesting only invoker-level elevation so 'it inherits the launching user's rights with no additional check'.

requirements.description: The system MUST NOT store, commit or distribute production personal data inside its source repository, build artefacts or deployment package, and MUST provide a documented, audited mechanism for purging personal data from any artefact in which it has been exposed.

acceptance_criteria.given: The repository and the build output
acceptance_criteria.then: No personal data is present, and the check fails any change that would add a datastore file or data export

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Purge mechanism exists and is audited
acceptance_criteria.given: An artefact found to contain exposed personal data
acceptance_criteria.when: The documented purge mechanism is invoked
acceptance_criteria.then: The data is removed from the artefact and from its history, and the action is recorded

requirements.anomaly_details: ESC-1 is an OPEN, CRITICAL, stakeholder-required escalation and the most serious single finding in the Discovery record. Its five evidence points are: the table stores names, guardian name, two telephone numbers and dates of birth for named individuals; the decode recovered real values from data pages, confirming a live dataset rather than an empty schema; zero authentication, authorization or encryption exists anywhere; a confirmed exploitable injection vector provides a live exfiltration path for the entire dataset; and the repository is a public project. The escalation rationale states the severity basis: 'this is an active, ongoing public exposure of real PII (not a latent or hypothetical risk)'. This requirement prescribes the forward control only — remediating the historical exposure is an action owned outside this SRS and is carried in srs.json open questions, since ESC-1 remains open with status open and no owner assigned.

requirements.description: The system MUST establish an authenticated session distinct from any datastore connection, MUST expire it after a configurable idle period and after a configurable absolute lifetime, and MUST clear any displayed personal data from the surface on expiry.

acceptance_criteria.given: An authenticated session displaying a student record, with an idle timeout of T
acceptance_criteria.when: No interaction occurs for longer than T
acceptance_criteria.then: The session is invalidated, the displayed personal data is cleared from the surface, and the next operation requires re-authentication

acceptance_criteria.given: A continuously active session with absolute lifetime L
acceptance_criteria.then: The session is invalidated

acceptance_criteria.given: The implementation
acceptance_criteria.then: It is independent of the lifetime of any datastore connection

requirements.anomaly_details: The identity assessment records that the legacy system had 'no application session concept at all, therefore no idle timeout, no maximum session lifetime, no re-authentication interval, and no short-lived token to expire', because the only session-like object was a connection opened on dashboard load and held for the lifetime of the process. Its consequence is stated plainly: 'An unattended workstation leaves the full PII CRUD surface live indefinitely.' The remediation explicitly warns against the obvious shortcut — 'Do not set the timeout at the connection layer — scope it to the authenticated session' — which is why the separation is written into the requirement. Concrete timeout values are client policy and require SME confirmation.

requirements.description: The system SHOULD require re-authentication or elevated assurance before a purge, an erasure or a bulk destructive operation, and MUST audit both the elevation and its outcome.

acceptance_criteria.given: An authenticated principal authorized to purge
acceptance_criteria.then: They are required to re-authenticate before it proceeds, and both the elevation and the purge are audited

acceptance_criteria.given: The same principal
acceptance_criteria.then: The purge does not proceed and the failed elevation is audited

acceptance_criteria.given: A create or amend
acceptance_criteria.then: No re-authentication is required, so the control does not impede ordinary work

requirements.anomaly_details: The identity assessment records the gap with a wry precision worth preserving: 'Destructive and PII-mutating operations require no elevated assurance. Record deletion is gated only by a Yes/No MessageBox, and record edit by no confirmation at all; neither re-authenticates, and since there is no authentication to begin with there is nothing to step up from.' Priority is should rather than must because the gap is rated medium and because the elevation scope is a client policy choice; the underlying authorization requirement in REQ-061 is must-strength regardless.

requirements.description: Every student record MUST carry created-at, created-by, modified-at, modified-by, version and lifecycle-state attributes, all maintained by the system from the server time source and the authenticated principal, and none editable by any principal through any path.

acceptance_criteria.given: A newly created record
acceptance_criteria.then: created_at and modified_at hold the server instant, created_by and modified_by hold the authenticated principal, row_version is 1 and lifecycle_state is Active

acceptance_criteria.given: An amendment to an existing record
acceptance_criteria.then: modified_at and modified_by update, row_version advances, and created_at and created_by are unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: A service call supplying values for any provenance attribute
acceptance_criteria.then: The supplied values are ignored and the system's own values are used

traces_to.line_note: students table definition; the absence is the finding.

requirements.anomaly_details: PRESCRIBED FROM A NAMED ABSENCE. BR-095 records that the legacy table had 'exactly ten business columns and no created-at, created-by, modified-at, modified-by, version or status column', so 'it is impossible to establish when a student record was created or last changed, who changed it, what the previous values were, or whether a student is current, graduated or withdrawn'. db-archaeology adds that the Access object-level design dates record when the table definition changed, not when any row changed, 'so they cannot substitute for row provenance'. These attributes are the precondition for REQ-058's concurrency token, REQ-027's retention and REQ-045's population scoping — none of which is representable without them.

requirements.description: The system MUST write an immutable audit entry for every create, amend, state transition, archive, purge, erasure and reference-data change, recording the acting principal, the instant, the operation and the prior and new values of each changed attribute. The entry MUST be written inside the same transaction as the change it describes.

acceptance_criteria.given: An amendment changing last name from 'Mehta' to 'Sharma'
acceptance_criteria.then: One audit entry records operation Update, the acting principal, the instant, and last name with prior value 'Mehta' and new value 'Sharma', and records no other attribute

acceptance_criteria.given: An amendment whose audit write fails
acceptance_criteria.then: Neither the amendment nor the audit entry persists

acceptance_criteria.given: An existing audit entry
acceptance_criteria.when: Any path attempts to modify or delete it
acceptance_criteria.then: The attempt fails and is itself audited

requirements.anomaly_details: PRESCRIBED FROM A NAMED ABSENCE. BR-095 records that 'only the ten business columns are written; no provenance, actor or version data is recorded anywhere' and that 'no log file, event record or history table is produced'. The data-flow assessment states the consequence at critical severity: 'Insert, update and delete leave no trace beyond the mutated row.' The same-transaction clause depends on REQ-057, because the legacy system had no transaction mechanism to write an audit entry inside — BR-093's note that 'any future multi-table operation would have no consistency mechanism to build on' is precisely this case.

requirements.description: Audit entries MUST be retained independently of the records they describe and MUST survive the purge of those records. Read access to audit entries MUST be separately authorized and MUST itself be audited.

acceptance_criteria.given: A purged student record
acceptance_criteria.when: The audit store is queried for its identifier
acceptance_criteria.then: Its complete audit history is present, including the purge entry

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal authorized to read student records but not audit entries
acceptance_criteria.then: It is denied and the denial is audited

acceptance_criteria.given: An authorized audit read
acceptance_criteria.then: An entry records who read which audit history and when

requirements.anomaly_details: Survival across purge is the specific property that makes REQ-027's logical deletion defensible: without it, purging a record would destroy the evidence that it ever existed and that someone destroyed it, which is the legacy posture under a new name. The separate authorization is prescribed because audit entries hold prior values of personal-data attributes and therefore inherit the highest classification in the data model — the data-domain assessment classifies the student cluster as 'PII — highest in the application' with observed access control of 'none'. BR-095's recorded consequence is the one this requirement closes: 'no create, update or delete in this system is attributable or reconstructible after the fact — a material constraint on any modernization that must demonstrate data lineage or support data-subject requests over this personal data'.

requirements.description: The system MUST support fulfilment of a data-subject request as a distinct, audited operation, and MUST allow the personal data of a guardian to be erased independently of the student record. Erasure MUST record its lawful basis and MUST NOT cascade to or from the student's own lifecycle.

acceptance_criteria.given: An Active student record with a guardian reference
acceptance_criteria.when: An authorized principal erases the guardian's personal data
acceptance_criteria.then: The guardian name is irrecoverably removed, erased_at is set, the student record remains Active and complete, and an audit entry with operation Erase persists

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Student purge does not discharge a guardian request
acceptance_criteria.given: A purged student record
acceptance_criteria.when: The guardian erasure register is checked
acceptance_criteria.then: Any outstanding guardian erasure request is still recorded as requiring action or as satisfied by the purge, explicitly rather than by implication

acceptance_criteria.given: A data-subject access request for a named student
acceptance_criteria.then: Every attribute held about that student, and its audit history, is retrievable in one audited operation

requirements.anomaly_details: The data-domain assessment identifies the guardian as a distinct data subject and describes the legacy position exactly: 'personal data about a second, unconsented data subject held inside the student's row, with no separate identity, no consent basis and no independent erasure path'. BR-095 records that 'record-level ownership and data-subject access rights cannot be implemented on this schema, which has no actor columns', and the data-flow assessment that the absence of any deletion or retention path 'forecloses both data-subject-request handling and any reconstruction after an erroneous delete'. SME confirmation is unavoidable here: the applicable obligations are a legal determination the data-domain assessment refers to a data-protection reviewer as an open question, and the governing profile's compliance configuration was not readable from this workspace, so no profile-supplied answer was available either.

requirements.description: The system MUST maintain a version token on every student record, advancing it on each persisted change, and MUST expose it to any client that retrieves the record so the client can submit it with an amendment.

acceptance_criteria.given: Any record retrieval
acceptance_criteria.then: It carries the current version token

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Token advances only on persisted change
acceptance_criteria.given: An amendment that changes at least one attribute, and separately one that changes none
acceptance_criteria.then: The token advances in the first case and does not in the second

acceptance_criteria.given: A create request supplying a version token
acceptance_criteria.then: The supplied value is ignored

requirements.anomaly_details: PRESCRIBED FROM A NAMED ABSENCE. BR-094 records that the legacy system had 'no optimistic concurrency token, no row version, no timestamp and no change detection', which is what made last-write-wins silent, and BR-095 confirms the schema carried no version column. This requirement is the data-side counterpart of REQ-058's behavioural rule: the token is what REQ-058 compares, so neither requirement is satisfiable alone.

requirements.description: After any successful mutation the system MUST refresh every presentation surface whose displayed data is affected, through an explicit declared notification contract. It MUST NOT address a surface implicitly by type name, and MUST NOT maintain more than one instance of a surface for the same logical view.

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal viewing the record list who creates a new record
acceptance_criteria.then: The visible list shows the new record and the visible statistics reflect it, with no further navigation required

acceptance_criteria.given: The running application after several navigations and mutations
acceptance_criteria.then: At most one exists per logical view, and no invisible duplicate exists

acceptance_criteria.given: The refresh implementation
acceptance_criteria.then: Affected surfaces are notified through a declared contract; no surface is reached by resolving its type name

requirements.anomaly_details: After a successful legacy create, the handler called two refresh methods by type name, invoking the framework's per-thread default instances. BR-019 records that one happened to work because that type's default instance was the visible main form, while the other 'constructs or reuses a second, invisible ViewForm, runs its Load handler, and refreshes a grid nobody can see. The visible grid is left stale.' The structural assessment rates this coupling critical and names the porting consequence: 'because C# has no default-instance feature any port must consciously re-establish the intended parent-child wiring'. The clinching evidence that the calls were unintentional is the contrast BR-078 records: the navigation handler reached the hosted instance correctly through a guarded cast, 'the one place in the application that correctly addresses the hosted instance rather than the VB default instance'. The hidden instance also opened a connection and bound a result set that was never disposed, accumulating redundant work on every create.

requirements.description: After a successful amendment the system MUST refresh the record list and the statistics through the same notification contract as every other mutation. The refresh MUST NOT depend on an event subscription registered by an unrelated component.

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal viewing the record list who amends a record's programme
acceptance_criteria.then: The list row and the programme statistics both update

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Refresh does not depend on a foreign subscription
acceptance_criteria.given: The refresh implementation
acceptance_criteria.then: It is invoked by the mutation's own notification, not as a side effect of a surface closing

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cancelling an amendment causes no datastore work
acceptance_criteria.given: A principal who opens a record and cancels
acceptance_criteria.then: No refresh query is issued, where the legacy cancel path triggered a full list reload

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy amendment refreshed the statistics by type name and then closed its surface. BR-038 records that 'the grid is not refreshed directly; it updates only because ViewForm attached a FormClosed handler when it launched the edit form' — so 'the refresh of the user's primary view therefore depends on an event subscription made in a different module, which is why the update path happens to work where the insert path does not'. It worked by accident, and the accident is why no two mutation paths agreed. BR-038 also records that cancelling still triggered the reload, 'so a cancelled edit still causes a database round trip', and that repeated launches re-registered the handler so the list reloaded once per accumulated subscription.

requirements.description: The system MUST apply one refresh contract uniformly to create, amend, archive and purge, with no path exempt, and MUST preserve any active filter across a refresh per REQ-023.

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal who archives a record
acceptance_criteria.then: Both the record list and the statistics update immediately, where the legacy delete path refreshed the list but never the statistics

acceptance_criteria.given: The four mutation operations
acceptance_criteria.when: Each is performed with both surfaces visible
acceptance_criteria.then: All four refresh both surfaces identically; no two paths differ

acceptance_criteria.given: An active filter and any mutation
acceptance_criteria.then: The filter is still applied

requirements.anomaly_details: IM-020 states the defect in one sentence: 'Three mutation paths have three mutually inconsistent refresh behaviours. Insert refreshes the dashboard but not the visible grid; delete refreshes the visible grid but not the dashboard; update refreshes both... No two of the three agree, and nothing in any single file describes the intended contract.' BR-058 adds that after a deletion the statistics 'remain at their pre-delete values until the user navigates Home — and because the delete also closed the shared connection, that navigation raises an unhandled exception instead', so the one route that would have corrected the figures crashed the application. The resolution is consolidation onto one contract rather than three separate fixes, because the divergence is itself the finding.

requirements.description: Event subscriptions MUST be symmetric: every subscription MUST have exactly one corresponding removal, and no component may accumulate duplicate subscriptions across a session. A single logical refresh MUST result in exactly one datastore read.

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal who opens and closes the amendment surface ten times in one session
acceptance_criteria.when: Subscriptions are counted after each close
acceptance_criteria.then: The count is the same each time, and the list reloads exactly once per close

acceptance_criteria.given: Any single logical refresh
acceptance_criteria.then: Exactly one read is issued for the affected surface

acceptance_criteria.given: The running application after extended navigation
acceptance_criteria.when: Retained presentation and data resources are enumerated
acceptance_criteria.then: None is unreachable from the current surface

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy amend-launch path attached a close handler on every click while constructing a new surface only when none existed or the previous was disposed. BR-062 records that 'because AddHandler is unconditional while construction is not, each reuse adds another subscription to the same event on the same instance', so 'the grid reload therefore runs once on the first edit, twice on the second, three times on the third, and so on, producing N redundant full-table queries and rebinds per close'. BR-062 is candid that the defect is latent today because both exit paths dispose the instance, and draws the right conclusion for a modernization specification: 'the reuse branch via UpdateRollNo is therefore rarely reached in practice, making this a latent rather than an everyday defect, and the dead reuse branch is itself a maintenance hazard'. ANOM-051 omits that dead branch; this requirement fixes the asymmetry that made it dangerous.

requirements.description: A presentation surface MUST NOT modify the structure, layout or control collection of another surface. Presentation of one surface within another MUST occur only through a declared composition mechanism owned by the containing surface.

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered codebase
acceptance_criteria.then: No surface adds to, removes from or reorders another surface's control structure

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Composition is owned by the container
acceptance_criteria.given: The amendment surface being presented within the shell
acceptance_criteria.then: The shell performs it in response to a declared request, not the list surface reaching into the shell

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No surface remains interactable beneath another
acceptance_criteria.given: The amendment surface presented
acceptance_criteria.when: The underlying list is probed for interaction
acceptance_criteria.then: It is not interactable, where the legacy list remained live and bound with stale data beneath the amendment surface

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy amend path did not open a dialog: it constructed the amendment surface, made it non-top-level and added it to the shell's host panel through the shell's default instance, 'reaching across module boundaries into the dashboard's control tree'. BR-063 records the resulting shape — 'the edit form is therefore a sibling of the view form inside the same host panel rather than a child of it, and the view form remains live and bound underneath' — and its complexity rationale names the defect precisely: 'a child module mutates the parent shell's control collection via a default instance, inverting the expected ownership direction'. This inversion is one of the three circular module dependency cycles the structural assessment rates high severity.

requirements.description: The set of events that trigger a statistics refresh MUST be declared and complete: every mutation that can change a reported figure MUST trigger one. No figure may be displayed as current when a mutation since its computation could have changed it.

acceptance_criteria.given: The declared trigger set
acceptance_criteria.when: It is compared against the set of mutations that can change a reported figure
acceptance_criteria.then: They are identical, with no mutation omitted

acceptance_criteria.given: A visible statistics surface and a principal who archives a record
acceptance_criteria.then: The figures refresh, where the legacy delete path triggered no statistics refresh at all

acceptance_criteria.given: A figure that could have been invalidated by another principal's change
acceptance_criteria.then: It carries an as-of instant or is marked stale per NFR-033

requirements.anomaly_details: BR-077 records that legacy statistics were recomputed 'on form load, on Dashboard navigation, after a successful insert and after a successful update — but not after a delete', and that 'there is no timer, no auto-refresh and no change notification, so with two application instances running neither sees the other's changes until it navigates'. Its summary is the requirement's rationale: 'the refresh set is therefore incomplete in one direction and stale in another'. One of the four working triggers reached the dashboard only by the default-instance coincidence described in REQ-070, so the legacy trigger set was not merely incomplete but partly accidental.

requirements.description: Navigation between surfaces MUST be an explicit declared state transition. Exactly one primary surface MUST be presented at a time, and a surface it replaces MUST be fully released, retaining no residual input state. Unsaved input MUST either be explicitly persisted as a draft or discarded with warning; it MUST NOT persist invisibly.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: One primary surface at a time
acceptance_criteria.given: A principal navigating between the dashboard, the list and the create surface
acceptance_criteria.then: Exactly one primary surface is presented and no previously presented surface remains layered beneath it

acceptance_criteria.given: A principal who enters data on the create surface, navigates away without saving, and returns
acceptance_criteria.then: They were warned on leaving, and the surface does not silently restore the abandoned input

acceptance_criteria.given: The application after navigating through every surface twice
acceptance_criteria.then: The count does not grow with navigation, where the legacy host panel accumulated child surfaces across the session

acceptance_criteria.given: The navigation implementation
acceptance_criteria.then: Each transition matches the NavigationContext state machine in srs.json, and no transition depends on testing whether an object was previously disposed

requirements.anomaly_details: BR-078 is the most complex single behaviour in the application, rated EXTREME complexity because it 'touches four modules and combines manual control reparenting, conditional instance reuse keyed on IsDisposed, z-order management, cross-module mutation of another form's control collection, and VB default-instance resolution. It is the substrate on which BR-019, BR-062 and BR-063 all depend and no single file describes it.' The legacy shell had no navigation at all: child surfaces were reparented into one host panel and merely hidden, so 'Panel5 permanently accumulates child form controls stacked over the still-present statistics tiles'. An amendment surface left hosted 'is hidden rather than closed, so its unsaved edits persist invisibly and reappear on return'. The structural assessment records that the shell and statistics concerns deliberately overlap on one module and that 'that overlap IS the finding', and directs that 'the parent-child refresh contract must be re-specified rather than translated' — hence SME confirmation on the intended navigation model.

requirements.description: The system MUST warn before discarding unsaved input on exit, MUST release every resource it holds on exit, and MUST provide a supported means of exiting that does not depend on a single bespoke control.

acceptance_criteria.given: An entry surface with unsaved input
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal exits by any supported route
acceptance_criteria.then: They are warned and may cancel

acceptance_criteria.given: Any surface
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal uses the platform's standard close affordance
acceptance_criteria.then: The application closes orderly

acceptance_criteria.given: A running instance holding datastore, session and lock resources
acceptance_criteria.then: Each is released explicitly rather than by process termination

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy shell removed the window's close, minimise and maximise chrome, so BR-079 records that 'the single Exit button is therefore the only supported way to terminate the application' and notes the fragility plainly: 'if the Exit handler were removed, the application would have no closure affordance at all'. Neither exit route prompted about unsaved data in a hosted entry surface, and neither closed the shared connection — 'the connection and the Access lock file are released only by process termination, not by an orderly close'. BR-056 records that exit is one of the destructive actions the legacy system never confirmed.

requirements.description: The system MUST distinguish validation failures, business-rule violations, concurrency conflicts, absent-record outcomes and infrastructure faults, and MUST present each with a distinct actionable message. Raw provider or runtime exception text MUST NOT be shown to a principal.

acceptance_criteria.given: A duplicate roll number, a telephone format violation, a version conflict, an archived target and an unreachable datastore
acceptance_criteria.then: Each produces a distinct message identifying its class and its remedy, and no two are presented identically

acceptance_criteria.given: Any failure
acceptance_criteria.then: It contains no runtime or provider exception text, no stack trace and no type name

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Infrastructure faults are not blamed on input
acceptance_criteria.given: An unreachable datastore during a create
acceptance_criteria.then: It is reported as a system fault the principal cannot remedy by changing their input

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy create path was wrapped in a single catch-all that displayed 'Error: ' concatenated with the raw runtime message. BR-022 records exactly what that cost: 'Duplicate-key violations, mobile-number overflows, provider failures, missing-dropdown null references and connection faults are all presented identically, so the user cannot distinguish a data-entry mistake from an infrastructure outage, and no record of the failure survives the dismissal of the message box.' Its complexity rationale is the clearest statement of the defect: the single catch block 'erases the diagnostic distinction between every failure mode in the system'. Worse, BR-022 records that an exception raised after the row had committed 'reports an error even though the row was committed, so the user is told the save failed when it did not'.

requirements.description: The system MUST apply one uniform error-handling policy implemented at the application boundary rather than per operation. No unhandled fault may terminate the process, and every acquired resource MUST be released deterministically on both the success and the failure path.

acceptance_criteria.given: Each operation in turn, with a fault injected into it
acceptance_criteria.then: The fault is reported, the application continues running, and no operation exists whose failure terminates the process

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Handling is uniform, not per handler
acceptance_criteria.given: The error-handling implementation
acceptance_criteria.then: One policy is applied at the boundary; comparable failures do not behave differently depending on which operation they occur in

acceptance_criteria.given: A fault mid-way through any resource-holding operation
acceptance_criteria.then: Every acquired resource is released, and the next operation is unaffected

requirements.anomaly_details: IM-029 records the asymmetry exactly: 'The insert and update handlers are wrapped in blanket Try/Catch blocks, while the record load, the grid load, the search, the delete, the edit launch and the dashboard statistics loader have no exception handling at all — so comparable failures either show a message box or terminate the process depending only on which path they occur in.' Six paths had none. BR-035 records that the amendment surface read the datastore inside its constructor with no guard, invoked from a handler with no guard, so 'every failure mode of the load path propagates as an unhandled exception and terminates the application'. The recovered navigation state machine lists an explicit transition to a Terminated state from any unhandled exception in the view, search, delete or amend-launch path. IM-029 also records 'there is no Using block or Finally anywhere', so the resource-release clause is a separate, equally necessary prescription — a parse failure left an open reader on the shared connection for the life of the process. This is CONSOLIDATE rather than FIX because the defect is not uniform neglect but six divergent behaviours.

requirements.description: Startup MUST validate that every required configuration value is present and resolvable and MUST fail with a diagnostic naming the missing or unresolvable setting. An unreachable datastore MUST be reported distinguishably from a missing configuration value, and neither may crash the application.

acceptance_criteria.given: A deployment with one required setting absent
acceptance_criteria.then: It reports that setting by name with the expected form of its value, logs the condition, and does not display a provider error

acceptance_criteria.given: A correctly configured but unreachable datastore
acceptance_criteria.then: It reports the datastore as unreachable, distinguishably from a configuration error, and starts without crashing

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No crash before a usable surface
acceptance_criteria.given: Any startup failure
acceptance_criteria.then: A surface is presented carrying the diagnostic; the application does not terminate before any window is usable

requirements.anomaly_details: BR-002's error paths are the legacy startup experience: 'Any other machine — OleDbException could not find file', drive absent or not writable, and a read-only directory failing because the engine must create a lock file even for read-only queries. BR-001 adds provider-not-installed and 64-bit-process failures. Because the statistics loader ran unguarded from the load handler, BR-076 records that all of these produced 'a crash on launch before any window is usable'. The three criteria here convert three indistinguishable crashes into three named, actionable diagnostics.

requirements.description: Validation failures MUST be reported together in one pass, each attributed to the specific field it concerns, expressed in terms of the expected form rather than the technical cause, and exposed to assistive technology in association with that field.

acceptance_criteria.given: A submission with three distinct validation failures
acceptance_criteria.then: All three are reported in one pass, each naming its field; the principal is not made to resubmit to discover the next

acceptance_criteria.given: A telephone number failing its format rule
acceptance_criteria.then: The message states the expected format, not the technical cause

acceptance_criteria.given: A field-level validation failure
acceptance_criteria.when: The surface is read by assistive technology
acceptance_criteria.then: The error is announced in association with its field, satisfying REQ-106

requirements.anomaly_details: The legacy system reported validation failures one at a time, as an exception, with no field attribution. BR-011 records that an unselected selector produced 'Error: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.' with 'no indication of the offending field', and that leaving gender, programme or admission year unselected produced 'identical, indistinguishable' messages. The accessibility audit records the same defect as A11Y-007 against WCAG 3.3.2, noting that 'the only error surfaced is a single generic MsgBox(ex.Message) not tied to the offending field'. BR-096 and BR-017 add that length and range violations surfaced the same way, 'with no indication that length was the problem'.

requirements.description: Every failure message shown to a principal MUST cite a correlation identifier that resolves to the structured log entry and, where applicable, the audit entry for the same operation.

acceptance_criteria.given: Any infrastructure or system failure
acceptance_criteria.then: It cites a correlation identifier that locates the structured log entry for that failure

acceptance_criteria.given: A failed operation that also produced an audit entry
acceptance_criteria.then: It resolves to both

acceptance_criteria.given: A field validation failure the principal can remedy
acceptance_criteria.then: The message is actionable without a correlation identifier, so routine corrections are not cluttered

requirements.anomaly_details: BR-022 records that the legacy system had 'no logging, no telemetry, no error code' and that 'no record of the failure survives the dismissal of the message box'. The correlation identifier is the mechanism that links a user-visible failure to a durable record of it, which is what makes REQ-080's failure classes diagnosable in operation rather than only in principle.

requirements.description: Every interactive and informational element MUST expose a programmatic name, and a programmatic description where the name alone is ambiguous, sufficient for assistive technology to identify and operate it without reference to visual layout. Purely decorative elements MUST be marked so assistive technology skips them. The system MUST satisfy WCAG 2.1 success criterion 4.1.2 at Level A.

acceptance_criteria.given: Every surface of the delivered system
acceptance_criteria.when: Each element is inspected for a programmatic name
acceptance_criteria.then: Every interactive and informational element has one, against a legacy baseline of zero across all 137 controls

acceptance_criteria.given: A compiled build and a screen reader
acceptance_criteria.when: A principal performs create, search, amend and archive using the screen reader with no sighted assistance
acceptance_criteria.then: Every operation completes and every control is identified by purpose

acceptance_criteria.given: A decorative image
acceptance_criteria.then: It is not announced

requirements.anomaly_details: This is the only CRITICAL accessibility finding and the one that forces the FAIL gate verdict. The audit verified a measured zero: neither of the two accessible-name properties occurs anywhere in any of the four Designer files, across 137 controls. Its assessment of the impact is why this requirement ranks first in MOD-010: the missing annotations are 'the only mechanism (keyboard + screen reader) a non-visual user has to operate the application at all', and the platform offers no label-association fallback. The audit's own remediation list places this first as 'the single highest-impact fix since it is currently a measured zero'. The decorative-element clause is the one place either artefact mentions success criterion 1.1.1, and it appears there only in remediation text — srs-accessibility-compliance.json records 1.1.1 as never formally assessed.

requirements.description: Data presented in tabular form MUST carry human-readable, fully expanded column labels exposed to assistive technology. Abbreviations MUST be expanded. The system MUST satisfy WCAG 2.1 success criteria 1.3.1 and 3.3.2 at Level A.

acceptance_criteria.given: The record list
acceptance_criteria.when: A screen reader announces its column labels
acceptance_criteria.then: It announces expanded terms such as 'Year of Admission' and 'First Name', not raw attribute tokens such as 'YOA' or 'FName'

acceptance_criteria.given: The record list
acceptance_criteria.then: The relationship between each value and its column label is programmatically determinable

requirements.anomaly_details: Rated SERIOUS. The legacy grid was bound to the raw table with automatic column generation and no explicit columns or header text, so headers rendered as the literal attribute names and 'a screen reader announces the raw DB token'. This finding is the only one in the audit mapped to two success criteria, 1.3.1 and 3.3.2. It is also the accessibility face of ANOM-043's naming inconsistency and of REQ-033's presentation-layer column declaration, so one change discharges three findings.

requirements.description: Information distinguishing one element or figure from another MUST NOT be conveyed by colour or image alone. Each reported figure MUST carry distinct text naming what it reports. The system MUST satisfy WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.4.1 at Level A.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cohort figures are distinguishable in text
acceptance_criteria.given: The cohort figures
acceptance_criteria.when: They are read with no access to colour or images
acceptance_criteria.then: Each is identified by distinct text naming its cohort, against a legacy baseline of five elements all captioned identically

acceptance_criteria.given: Every surface rendered in greyscale
acceptance_criteria.then: No information is lost

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Labels are derived from the data
acceptance_criteria.given: A change to the number of cohort buckets per REQ-043
acceptance_criteria.then: Their labels follow automatically rather than requiring a separate text edit

requirements.anomaly_details: Rated SERIOUS. All five legacy cohort elements carried the identical caption, with the ordinal carried solely by a decorative coloured numeral image, none of which had an accessible name — so the five figures were indistinguishable non-visually. IM-033 records the same defect from the business-logic side and adds that no string literal for any ordinal exists anywhere in the file: the distinction 'is carried solely by picture-box image resources and by control names, so the tiles are not distinguishable from their text, not localizable and not greppable'. The third criterion links this to REQ-043: deriving the labels from the reference data is what keeps them correct when the bucket count changes.

requirements.description: Focus order MUST be unique, deterministic and documented on every surface, and MUST follow the surface's logical reading and operation order. No two elements on a surface may declare the same focus position. The system MUST satisfy WCAG 2.1 success criterion 2.4.3 at Level A.

acceptance_criteria.given: Every surface
acceptance_criteria.then: Each is unique, against a legacy baseline of two duplicate pairs in the navigation rail

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Order is verified against a build
acceptance_criteria.given: A compiled build
acceptance_criteria.when: A principal traverses each surface by keyboard alone
acceptance_criteria.then: Focus follows the documented logical order with no unexpected jump and no element skipped

acceptance_criteria.given: Any surface
acceptance_criteria.when: A principal traverses it by keyboard alone
acceptance_criteria.then: Focus can always move onward and away; no element traps it

requirements.anomaly_details: In the legacy navigation rail the Report and View buttons both declared focus position 6 and the Insert and Dashboard buttons both declared 7, making keyboard focus order 'ambiguous/implementation-defined'. The third criterion is prescribed because srs-accessibility-compliance.json records an unassessed gap here: the audit could not determine from source alone whether the duplicate positions and the overlapping panels 'produce an actual keyboard trap or merely an inefficient tab order', so the modernized system must be verified rather than reasoned about.

requirements.description: No element may remain in the focus order or the accessibility tree that is not intended to be presented. Meaningful sequence MUST be programmatically determinable and MUST match the visual presentation order. The system MUST satisfy WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.3.2 at Level A.

acceptance_criteria.given: Every surface
acceptance_criteria.when: A principal traverses it with assistive technology
acceptance_criteria.then: Only intended elements are encountered, against a legacy baseline in which two duplicate dashboard elements remained in the control collection and the focus order

acceptance_criteria.given: Any surface
acceptance_criteria.when: The programmatic sequence is compared with the visual order
acceptance_criteria.then: They match

acceptance_criteria.given: Any surface at any size
acceptance_criteria.then: No element overlaps another, where a legacy duplicate overlapped a real statistic element

requirements.anomaly_details: The two leftover duplicate dashboard elements are OMITTED from the SRS as dead code under ANOM-049, and this requirement is why the omission must be a REMOVAL rather than a hiding. The audit records that they were nested in the wrong parent at relative offsets resolving to absolute positions one of which overlapped a real statistic element, and that because they 'remain in the control collection and tab order, a keyboard/SR user can land on 0, BCA Students, IIMCA Students out of sequence'. BR-081 and IM-032 record that they were concealed only by being pushed outside their parent's bounds, so any layout change would expose them — which is also why NFR-051 forbids geometry-based concealment.

requirements.description: Every foreground and background colour pair MUST be an explicitly chosen fixed value, MUST NOT be inherited from an operating-system theme, and MUST be verified with a contrast-measurement tool against the Level AA minimum before release, with the measured ratio recorded. The system MUST satisfy WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.4.3 at Level AA.

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered surfaces
acceptance_criteria.then: No foreground or background colour is drawn from a system theme

acceptance_criteria.given: Every colour pair in the delivered system
acceptance_criteria.when: Its ratio is measured with a contrast tool
acceptance_criteria.then: Each meets or exceeds the Level AA minimum and the measured ratio is recorded, including pairs the legacy audit judged likely to pass without measuring

acceptance_criteria.given: The system under high-contrast mode
acceptance_criteria.then: All text and controls remain legible and all ratios still meet Level AA

requirements.anomaly_details: Two legacy elements used a theme-dependent system colour rather than a fixed value, so contrast against hardcoded black text 'is not fixed or verifiable at design time' and could fail Level AA under a different theme, accent colour or high-contrast mode. The audit was careful about the limits of its own evidence, calling this 'a qualitative, source-grounded flag, not a measured failure' and stating that it 'did not pixel-sample the screenshot or measure an exact ratio, and says so explicitly rather than asserting a fabricated number'.
