The second criterion deliberately extends beyond the two flagged elements because the audit's favourable judgement on the remaining pastel pairs was equally unmeasured, and because high-contrast and theme interactions are named among the things its method could not detect at all.

requirements.description: Every input MUST declare its expected format, maximum length and mandatory status at the surface, both visibly and programmatically, before submission. Every validation failure MUST be announced in association with the specific field it concerns. The system MUST satisfy WCAG 2.1 success criterion 3.3.2 at Level A.

acceptance_criteria.given: Each input on the create and amend surfaces
acceptance_criteria.when: The surface is read visually and by assistive technology
acceptance_criteria.then: Its expected format, maximum length and mandatory status are discoverable before submission, against a legacy baseline of zero declared maximum lengths

acceptance_criteria.given: A field-level validation failure
acceptance_criteria.when: The surface is read by assistive technology
acceptance_criteria.then: The error is announced in association with its field, not as a surface-level generic message

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Length is enforced at the surface
acceptance_criteria.given: An input with a declared maximum
acceptance_criteria.when: The principal attempts to exceed it
acceptance_criteria.then: The surface prevents the excess and announces the limit

requirements.anomaly_details: The audit verified that the maximum-length property occurs zero times in either entry Designer file and that neither code-behind performed field-specific validation, so 'the only error surfaced is a single generic MsgBox(ex.Message) not tied to the offending field'. Its conclusion is the requirement: assistive-technology users 'get no advance format/length cue and no field association on failure'. This finding is the accessibility face of three business-logic findings at once — the absent input validation, the schema-only length cap and the blanket exception handler — so REQ-003, REQ-009 and REQ-083 together satisfy it, and none of them alone does.

requirements.description: Every command control SHOULD expose a keyboard accelerator, and no two controls reachable on the same surface may share one. All functionality MUST remain operable by keyboard alone without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes. The system MUST satisfy WCAG 2.1 success criterion 2.1.1 at Level A.

acceptance_criteria.given: Every command control on a surface
acceptance_criteria.then: Each has one and no two on the same surface collide, against a legacy baseline of none anywhere

acceptance_criteria.given: A compiled build
acceptance_criteria.when: A principal performs every operation using the keyboard alone
acceptance_criteria.then: Every operation completes with no timing-dependent keystroke

requirements.anomaly_details: Rated MINOR, and the priority of the accelerator clause reflects that. The audit verified that no button caption in any of the four surfaces contains a mnemonic marker and was careful to bound the impact: 'All buttons remain reachable via Tab, so this is not a blocking keyboard failure', though the accelerator path relied on by keyboard-only and some motor-impaired principals is absent and the omission 'is inconsistent with typical Windows desktop-app conventions'. The full-keyboard-operability clause is must-strength because that is the substance of success criterion 2.1.1; only the accelerator convenience is should-strength.

requirements.description: Headings and labels MUST describe their topic or purpose. Element identifiers SHOULD denote purpose and actual type rather than being auto-generated, and SHOULD be unique within their surface. User-visible text MUST be correctly spelled and MUST NOT contain development-time or authorship residue. The system MUST satisfy WCAG 2.1 success criterion 2.4.6 at Level AA.

acceptance_criteria.given: The delivered codebase
acceptance_criteria.then: None is auto-generated or sequentially numbered, none is reused across surfaces, and none implies a type it does not have

acceptance_criteria.given: Every user-visible string
acceptance_criteria.then: It is correctly spelled and contains no author name, cohort label or placeholder comment

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Assistive technology never announces an internal name
acceptance_criteria.given: Every element
acceptance_criteria.then: It announces the purpose-describing accessible name from REQ-100, never an internal identifier

requirements.anomaly_details: Rated MINOR, and the audit is precise about why: legacy visible captions were descriptive so '2.4.6 is largely satisfied at the visual layer', and the generic internal names harmed principals only in combination with the critical missing accessible names, 'where UIA may expose the literal internal name (e.g. PictureBox14, cmbyoa) to a screen reader'. The audit accordingly rates the remediation 'low priority relative to A11Y-001', and the third criterion reflects that dependency: satisfying REQ-100 removes the mechanism by which this finding causes harm. Two user-visible defects are nonetheless must-strength: the legacy dashboard title was misspelled and a second label hardcoded the original author's name and cohort. IM-022 records a related trap — the ten statistics controls carried txt prefixes implying text boxes while being labels, 'so any future code that casts them or sets ReadOnly on them will fail'.

by_module.MOD-011_note: MOD-011 (Configuration and Deployment) carries no functional requirement of its own. Its behaviour is prescribed by REQ-051 and REQ-082, which are assigned to MOD-005 and MOD-009 because they are a persistence binding and a startup diagnostic respectively, and by NFR-015, NFR-022, NFR-023 and NFR-024 in the non-functional set. The module is retained in srs.json because the anomalies it owns — the hardcoded path, the unused settings store and the committed personal data — need a home.

totals.requirements_with_no_anomaly_note: Five requirements carry no anomaly resolution because they are not corrections. REQ-028 and REQ-024 make an existing cardinality and an existing gap explicit without changing behaviour; REQ-095, REQ-062 and REQ-063 prescribe capabilities with no legacy counterpart at all, traced to named absences rather than to observed defects. Note that REQ-028's and REQ-024's anomaly_resolution fields do name a resolution where one applies to a related finding; the five listed here are those whose primary content is not a correction.

business_rule_coverage.note: Every one of the 60 rules in business-logic.json is cited by at least one requirement in this file, either as its primary trace or as a corroborating finding. Three rules (BR-080, BR-081, BR-062 in part) resolve to OMIT and are cited by a requirement that records the omission and its justification rather than prescribing the behaviour — BR-080 by REQ-047, BR-081 by REQ-048, and BR-062's dead reuse branch by REQ-073 with the omission itself in ANOM-051. The full rule-to-requirement mapping is in srs.json traceability_matrix.
